[CI][EPLB] Revert #17579 to diagnose Qwen3-235B PD decoder startup (#23274)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Reverts #17579 on main `6e1ed5a7` to test whether the EPLB changes
contribute to the Qwen3-235B A3 PD decoder startup failure. In the
original run, decoder workers had EPLB enabled and failed during
piecewise graph capture. The device log reported an unresolved kernel
name in SuperKernel optimization. [Original failing
job](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45572445719/job/139062848261)

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Restores the previous EPLB map and record kernels and removes map warmup
registration introduced by #17579.

### How was this patch tested?

Verified the restored kernel file matches the parent of #17579 and ran
`git diff --check`. The target nightly case is
`QWEN3_235B_PD_3_5K_1_5k`. The original run used vLLM-Ascend `7dcdb690`;
this diagnostic PR uses a newer main baseline.

[Performance] Integrate union GBSA prefill for Qwen4Exp (#21627)

Fuse sparse-index preparation for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GBSA Prefill and
call the official GBSA metadata and attention operators.

## Performance results

### 128K input / 1-token output

#### A3

Both versions used the same Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A8 weights, 8 A3 NPUs
(TP2×PP4), and the same PP4 fixes. TTFT was averaged over the same five
requests per version after warm-up at concurrency 1. The measured prefix
cache hit rate was **88.87%** for both versions.

| Metric | Unit | Before (main) | After (GBSA Union) | Change | Change
rate |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT | ms | 1935.8 | 1699.0 | −236.7 | **−12.23%** |

#### A5

Both versions used the same Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A8-MXFP weights, 4 A5
NPUs (TP2×DP2, PP1), and the same operator runtime dependencies, with EP
enabled and MTP disabled. TTFT was averaged over the same five requests
per version after warm-up at concurrency 1. The measured prefix cache
hit rate was **88.87%** for both versions. All requests completed
successfully.

| Metric | Unit | Before (main) | After (GBSA Union) | Change | Change
rate |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT | ms | 2278.4 | 1938.5 | −339.9 | **−14.92%** |

The A5 comparison used main commit `03f69b977` and PR commit
`c02252e80`. A3 and A5 results are platform-specific comparisons; their
different parallel configurations do not support a direct comparison of
absolute latency across platforms.

### Full QSA module performance

Q=4096, KV=128K, TP2×PP1, including projections, LI V2, attention, and
TP communication.

| Platform | main | PR #21627 | Latency reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A3 | 22.858 ms | 16.875 ms | **26.17%** |
| A5 | 22.799 ms | 12.629 ms | **44.61%** |

Module tests use production weights and synthetic hidden states; these
are not end-to-end TTFT results.

### GPQA Diamond accuracy

The GBSA Union version was evaluated on all 198 questions with Thinking
enabled and the official recommended sampling parameters.

#### A3

Evaluated using 8 A3 NPUs (TP2×PP4).

| method | Correct | Incorrect | Accuracy | Truncated responses |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GPQA | 179/198 | 19 | **90.40%** | 2 |

One truncated response was scored as correct because the answer
extractor matched the expected choice in the unfinished Thinking text.

#### A5

Evaluated using 4 A5 NPUs (TP2×DP2, PP1).

| method | Correct | Incorrect | Accuracy | Truncated responses |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GPQA | 183/198 | 15 | **92.42%** | 1 |

The truncated response was scored as incorrect.

The A5 GPQA run used the image’s standard GBSA runtime, while the A5
TTFT runs used isolated GBSA/metadata runtime dependencies. The GPQA
result therefore does not validate the exact operator runtime
configuration used for the A5 TTFT comparison.

TP2×PP4 end-to-end testing requires the PP4 fixes from #20443.

commits.message:
[Feature][Model] Enable Qwen3.8 Flash Next PP and SP (#20311)

## Summary

Enable Qwen3.8 Flash Next (Qwen4-Exp) pipeline parallelism (PP),
sequence parallelism (SP/FlashComm1), MTP speculative decoding, and
pipeline-disaggregated three-tier KV-cache pooling on Model Runner V2.

This is a thin current-`main` adaptation. The PR is validated with vLLM
main commit
[`c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15).

## Design and changes

### Qwen3.8 Next PP, SP, and MTP

- Enable FlashComm1/SP for Qwen3.8 Flash Next.
- Preserve PP-stage ownership across model state and intermediate-tensor
transport.
- Keep the optimized target-model QSA fused RMSNorm + MRoPE projection
while selecting the graph-safe decomposition for `mtp.` draft layers.
This avoids sending the MTP drafter through the target-only projection
path and prevents Q/K NaNs and draft-acceptance regressions.
- Size packed QSA/GDN/PLE cache slots for the largest physical state
group and allow a global cache group to have no local layers on a PP
stage.
- Use persistent request-slot indexing for Mamba state copies so
reordered or sparse batches cannot read or write another request's
SSM/conv state.

### Minimal MRV2 token alignment

`pad_num_tokens()` is the single policy entry that computes the physical
token-row count required by TP-shared execution.

- Graph initialization aligns each capture size before constructing
graph grids.
- Eager execution aligns `num_scheduled_tokens` before DP
synchronization and batch-descriptor construction.
- The scheduler retains the logical token limit while runner buffers and
graph capacity use the aligned physical limit. With TP4 and a logical
limit of 4097, the scheduler admits at most 4097 real tokens and the
physical capacity is 4100 rows.
- `batch_req_state.num_tokens` remains the logical count and
`batch_desc.num_tokens` remains the selected physical execution width.
- Padding rows in `input_ids` and `positions` are zeroed before full
physical buffers are consumed.

Padding is not moved into model-specific SP/PCP code, and
scheduler-visible request capacity is unchanged.

### Generic PP-local cache-group projection for AscendStore

vLLM preserves global KV-cache group IDs across workers while a
worker-local projection may legitimately contain `layer_names=[]`.
AscendStore now follows that contract without identifying PLE or a
particular model:

- `project_group_ids()` maps request-global group IDs to groups with
real local regions before synchronous GET, asynchronous PUT, and
asynchronous GET build transfer descriptors. Empty local groups never
produce `layerNum=0` descriptors.
- `_collect_group_pp_ranks()` gathers which PP ranks own each global
group. Lookup keys are generated only for real owners, preventing false
misses on keys that a non-owner PP rank never wrote.
- Global group order and IDs remain unchanged; only each worker's
physical I/O view is projected.

This is generic for any model whose global cache group is empty on some
PP stages, including singleton PLE and future layouts.

### Torch utility adaptation

The common `get_npu_view_from_cpu_tensor` behavior is provided through
the Ascend patch layer, with behavioral tests for the bound Core
function, operator call, and pinned-memory validation.

## Relationship to cache-group interleaving (#22327)

[#22327](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/22327) is
already in the current base. It changes compatible Qwen3.8 Next GDN
owners from contiguous chunks to `members[i::num_groups]`. Under
standard continuous PP partitioning, ordinary GDN groups are distributed
across every stage (`6/6` for PP2 and `3/3/3/3` for PP4), instead of
producing layouts such as `13/0` or `0/10`.

#22327 improves ordinary-group distribution. This PR independently makes
the AscendStore connector honor the general vLLM contract that a global
group may still be empty on a worker.

## Validation

### Unit and static checks

- Related CPU unit-test set before the final rebase: **497 passed, 2
skipped**.
- Current rebased head: pre-commit, Ruff/formatting, three-version mypy,
DCO, conflict checks, test selection, documentation builds, and both CPU
UT matrices pass.
- The selected NPU CI matrix is still running.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- The PR remains one signed-off commit on top of current `main`.

commits.message:
[BugFix][PCP] Compact decoder replay across PCP ranks on prefix hits (#22453)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #22416.

With prefill context parallelism (`PCP > 1`), prefix caching and
`--swa-bounded-replay`, a cache hit can return an immediate EOS
(`token_ids=[1]`)
instead of the expected continuation. Cold prefills and PCP=1 hits are
fine.

Root cause: `DecoderReplayState._pcp_kept_lengths` decides whether the
compact
decoder replay saves rows by comparing the **global** kept row count
with the
**PCP rank-local** padded token extent:

```python
num_padded = int(global_kept.sum())                 # 128
if num_padded >= batch.num_tokens_after_padding:    # 30 on PCP8
    return None
```

A prefix hit schedules the hit's last replay window plus the uncached
tail, and
PCP spreads that query across ranks (e.g. 234 tokens -> 24-30 rows per
rank on
PCP8). The global window (128) is therefore larger than the local padded
width
(30), so the function returns `None`, the compact replay is skipped, and
layers
21-39 run in the ordinary PCP main pass with the scheduler's replay
floor
instead of the compact replay floor. Cold prefills (local width ~1246)
and
PCP=1 hits (local width 234) take the compact replay, which is why only
PCP>1
hits break.

This PR removes the rank-local comparison. Compaction is a global
decision:
if any request is trimmed, the PCP branch compacts, the same rule the
non-PCP
path uses (`requires_compaction`). The rank-local padded width is not a
valid
proxy for it.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This is a correctness fix for an existing opt-in feature
(`swa_bounded_replay` with `PCP > 1`). Prefix caching off and PCP=1 are
inert:
`DecoderReplayState` is only constructed when bounded replay is enabled,
and
`_pcp_kept_lengths` returns early when there is no PCP context. No
release note
fragment is needed.

### How was this patch tested?

Tests in `tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_state.py`:

- `_pcp_kept_lengths` on a prefix hit split across PCP ranks (PCP2 and
PCP4,
with `local_token_indices`), where each rank's padded width is no larger
than
the global replay window. It checks the kept rows per rank, including
the
  owner of the tail, the rank before it, and a rank that owns none.
- A `prepare()`-level test (without stubbing `_pcp_kept_lengths`)
asserting that
the same prefix hit reaches the compact PCP replay (`layers.rows` is
set).

Both fail with the old rank-local comparison.

End-to-end validation on 16x 910B2C (A2), TP1 / DP2 / PCP8 / EP16, 1M
context,
MBT 16384, utilization 0.93, `--enable-prefix-caching
--swa-bounded-replay`:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 8K passphrase cold | `Q7X-4921-KLM.` | `Q7X-4921-KLM.` |
| 8K passphrase hit | EOS, `token_ids=[1]` | `Q7X-4921-KLM` |
| 32K passphrase cold | `Q7X-4921-KLM.` | `Q7X-4921-KLM.` |
| 32K passphrase hit | EOS | identical to cold, ids
`[51,25,58,15,25880,19,12496,39851,16,1]` |

After the fix, the hit trace takes the compact replay
(`uses_pcp_replay=True`, `replay_start=[9834]`).

The unit tests in this file pass on CPU. `ruff check`, `ruff format`,
and the
repository pre-commit hooks pass on the two changed files.

### Checklist

- [x] **Regression test**: added tests that fail with the old rank-local
  comparison and pass with the fix.
- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: the tests cover PCP ownership
of the
  replay window (owner of the tail, owner before it, no owner) and the
`prepare()` wiring; the existing tests cover owner-before-tail,
owner-of-tail,
  and prompt-logprob rows (no compaction).
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: not applicable to this pure
planning
  calculation.
- [x] **Performance impact**: cold prefills keep the ordinary replay
unless
compacting actually reduces rows on each rank. The decision now compacts
when
a trimmed request has cached context (a prefix hit spreads the replay
window
across PCP ranks and must be re-indexed) or when the global kept width
is
smaller than one PCP rank's shard width (`ceil(global_extent /
pcp_size)`),
a global value so every rank in the group makes the same decision. A
short
cold prefill (e.g. 129 tokens on PCP8 with a 128-token window) stays at
18
  local rows instead of padding
every rank to 128. On prefix hits compaction pads each rank to the
global
kept width; that is the existing PCP replay contract, and
`all_reduce(MAX)`
  of the per-rank kept widths remains a follow-up.

[Performance][Qwen4Exp] Write GBSA results directly to caller output (#22375)

## What this PR optimizes

Generic Block Sparse Attention previously allocated its own output
tensor and the QSA caller copied that same-shape result into the
graph-owned attention buffer, producing an extra TensorMove after GBSA.

This PR adds a caller-owned output path so GBSA writes directly into the
final attention buffer.

The branch is based directly on `upstream/main` at
`c12397a088f7e63ed9defae66ac98faffee88b81` and has no dependency on
#22373 or any GDN PR.

## Optimization points

- Add `npu_generic_block_sparse_attention_out` to the C++ ACLNN adapter.
- Validate caller output shape, dtype, device, and contiguity before
dispatch.
- Register PrivateUse1 and Meta implementations for the out variant.
- Add a Python `generic_block_sparse_attention_out` wrapper while
preserving the existing allocating API.
- Update the Qwen4Exp GBSA caller to pass its graph-owned output buffer
directly.
- Remove the post-GBSA `output.copy_(result)` path that generated the
same-shape TensorMove.
- Keep softmax-LSE behavior and the existing API available for other
callers.

## Scope boundaries

- No QSA metadata preparation or Indexer multi-stream changes.
- No GDN changes.
- Includes the required user-facing performance release note in
`release_notes/fragments/22375.yaml`.

## Validation

- Python bytecode compilation for all three changed Python files:
passed.
- `ruff format --check`: passed.
- `ruff check`: passed.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`: passed.
- Pairwise `git merge-tree --write-tree` checks against every other
functional branch completed without conflicts; no stacked PR is
required.

C++ build, A5 numerical comparison, ACL Graph replay, and profiler
confirmation that the GBSA-output TensorMove is absent remain required
before merge.

[BugFix][KVTransfer] Fix Mooncake group selection and PP reformat (#18476)

### What this PR does / why we need it

When P and D use different KV-head partitions, Mooncake must reformat
the received KV blocks before decode can use them. Two receiver bugs can
break this conversion:

- Cache selection parsed model layer numbers across all caches, allowing
a single-tensor index cache to enter a two-tensor K/V reformat group, or
omitting draft caches with reassigned transfer indices. Select the exact
registered transfer group's names and indices, intersected with the
current layer subset.
- Pending reformat descriptors were assigned by request ID and CP shard.
Multiple P PP stages contributing different layers to the same shard
overwrote each other's descriptors, leaving only the last stored segment
to be reformatted. Accumulate every PP segment under the existing lock
and retain the existing all-pulls-complete barrier, consume-once
behavior, and failure cleanup.

The second bug can return HTTP 200 with incorrect output because the KV
bytes arrive but some layers retain the transfer layout. PP4-to-PP1
alone does not require head-layout conversion; the reproduced case is P
TP4/PP4 to D TP2/PP1.

### Validation

- 34 targeted CPU regressions passed with the actual PR connector
imported in an existing Ascend runtime: 25 PP regressions plus the
original 9 cache-group selection cases.
- Negative control: the same 25 PP cases all fail on the unmodified PR
head.
- PP cases cover all 24 PP4 registration orders, two CP shards,
consume/clear exactly once, concurrent writers, and request isolation.
- Ruff lint and format checks passed for the changed connector and new
test.
- The same accumulation fix was previously validated on 2026-11-18 on
Ascend A3, with P TP4/PP4 and D TP2/DP16 across two decode hosts,
retaining MRV2, EAGLE3 and D FULL_DECODE_ONLY: 20/20 functional PD
requests correct (12/20 with only the group-selection fix), including
two long-input string retrieval cases; paired cold-cache
PD/local-prefill checks 4/4 correct. This was functional validation, not
a performance or GPQA result.
- Rebased the three existing fix/test commits unchanged onto main
`e445f28a29597aefe85b14abb72eea8a326b3082` on 2026-11-25 (`git
range-diff` confirms patch equivalence).
- Full CPU CI on rebased head `cdcf93b7a34b185883aa8b0fa376520bad29d097`
passed: [vLLM main
`c410543d`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45563750944/job/139034939276):
**22,889 passed, 131 skipped**; [vLLM
v0.34.0](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45563750944/job/139034939205):
**22,884 passed, 136 skipped**. Each lane passed all 34 PR-specific
regressions.
-
[Pre-commit](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45563750944/job/139033414828),
including format/lint and Python 3.10/3.11/3.12 type checks, and DCO
passed on this head. The hardware figures above remain the earlier
validation; no new NPU run is claimed for this rebase.

### User-facing change

Keep heterogeneous cache groups separate and reformat all transferred PP
layer segments before reporting receive completion. No new flags or
wire-format changes.

[Feature][Model] Add Kimi fine-grained projection and shared-expert TP (#21624) ### What this PR does / why we need it? Reduce per-device Kimi-K3.1 projection and shared-expert weight storage by sharding selected weights over independent DP-axis groups. Attention, convolution and recurrent state remain on the original request owner. - **Reuse GLM projection infrastructure:** GLM and Kimi share input-capacity preparation and QKV/beta owner restoration through `KDAInputProjectionTPLayout`. GLM retains its fused projection, owner-local F/G work and eager execution. GLM checks KDA head divisibility during startup configuration validation. The same configuration block accepts Kimi-K3.1 by its outer model type, and Kimi checks its head layout in the KDA layer. - **Keep Kimi-specific computation local:** mixed MXFP8 QKV and BF16 beta/F/G loading and multistream scheduling stay in the existing Kimi implementation. Kimi KDA localTP runs directly in the layer for full-graph decode. The main stream runs QKV input quantization, QKV quantized matmul and BF16 beta projection consecutively in that order. At the first recurrent KDA or RecoverSSM kernel, the auxiliary stream computes G and exchanges its head shards. The main stream joins before gated normalization. An idle owner still participates in the gate collective. DSA joins its gate after attention. Both paths use the common head layout. Existing KDA Column/Merged linears accept an explicit group and retain their loaders; no duplicate projection Linear classes or new `ops/finegrained_tp.py` file remain. - **Reuse output/public paths:** Public SFA detects the selected `OProjRowParallelOp` and uses the pre-trim token capacity for its existing exchange and reduction. GLM and Kimi SFA ranks with uneven batches or no local queries join the same O collectives. LM head, embedding and dense MLP retain their existing common execution paths, without chunk executors or Kimi-specific MLP/embedding graph operators. - **Shared experts:** partition gate/up outputs and matching down inputs, gather owner inputs, reuse scheme-owned quantization/local MLP, then perform one RS(sum) back to each owner. Linears do not repeat activation collectives. Models without latent transforms use the common runner; Kimi retains its latent-projection scheduling windows. Routed EP remains independent. Equal-size DP-axis groups reuse one coordinator; teardown destroys aliases once. The old active graph check stays in input preparation. A small inherited idle check covers both default and Mamba model-state entries before collectives; no dynamic `cudagraph_manager` attribute, dispatch callback or warmup context is added. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Seven independent sizes under `additional_config.finegrained_tp_config`, defaulting to 1; 0/1 disable a split: ```json { "finegrained_tp_config": { "qkv_iproj_tensor_parallel_size": 8, "gproj_tensor_parallel_size": 8, "oproj_tensor_parallel_size": 8, "mlp_tensor_parallel_size": 8, "embedding_tensor_parallel_size": 8, "lmhead_tensor_parallel_size": 8, "shared_expert_tensor_parallel_size": 8 }, "enable_shared_expert_dp": false, "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true, "scheduler_config": {"recompute_scheduler_enable": true} } ``` This is additional configuration, not a complete launch command. Configure the KV connector chain separately. - Sizes must divide DP size. The existing MoE-only restriction remains because dense workers do not preserve the required DP group. Projection knobs require model-side wiring. - GLM QKV-only retains TP=PCP=PP=1 and PD decode with explicit DP capacity padding. Kimi-specific graph and offload requirements do not apply to it. - Kimi QKV/G and shared TP require TP=PCP=DCP=PP=1, graph-dispatched PD decode, capture coverage including speculative slots, recompute scheduling and `PreemptOffloadConnector`. - Shared TP requires recognized partitioned gate/up/down linears and rejects shared-DP replication and LoRA. Fused shared MegaMoe stays disabled because its interface does not own the DP-axis AG/RS; routed MegaMoe remains independent. - Existing O/dense-MLP warning-and-disable behavior for insufficient capture coverage remains. Vocabulary topology/layout restrictions remain. Runtime idle MM ranks still join embedding collectives, preserving the captured buffer address. DSpark uses the DP-agreed query-pass decision when vocabulary TP is enabled; target projection synchronization does not pull dense drafters into unrelated collectives. These are required by the basic collective paths, independently of chunking. ### How was this patch tested? - At `929bb62f0e`, `python3 -m pytest -q tests/ut/ops/test_kimi_kda.py` passed all 168 tests, including the parameterized localTP stream-order checks. #### A5 EP64 weight savings from localTP8 On the eight-node A5 decode setup (64 NPUs, DP64 / TP1 / DCP1 / EP64), each fine-grained group has eight ranks. [Performance] Start layerwise KV prefetch after connector wait (#23107)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Split the layerwise AscendStore attention gate into independent load and
save gates. After `wait_for_kv_layer_from_connector()` returns, the load
gate can release future-layer prefetch without recording the current
layer's save event. The save gate still records the existing KV-ready
event at the attention boundary and submits the current-layer save
there. Recurrent layers retain their post-compute save path.

The connector wait opens the prefetch gate only for layerwise
AscendStore connectors, including when wrapped by a MultiConnector. The
attention boundary remains an idempotent fallback for callers that do
not open the load gate earlier.

after the current layer load completes. This changes transfer timing; no
measured latency or throughput gain is claimed. The release note is in

commits.message:
[BugFix] Fix DeepSeek V4.1 pipeline-parallel metadata and vision loading (#22823)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Deferred A5 MLA metadata tasks can execute in learned first-consumption
order rather than builder creation order. A ratio-1 task running before
the designated ratio-2 refresher can hit `assert visible is not None`,
or consume visibility retained from a previous execution.

Let the first nonzero-ratio task actually executed compute visibility,
and retain reuse only within the same builder closure and executor
submission. A fresh submission identity forces recomputation for
subsequent submissions, including capture after warmup. Synchronous
calls outside an executor recompute conservatively. Task ordering,
events, PP partitioning and the visibility formula are unchanged.

The module-level `ContextVar` holds only a submission identity, not a
tensor or a process-wide batch cache. Its lifetime is the synchronous
producer submission; `finally` restores the previous
thread/context-local value on success or failure, including nested
scopes. Visibility tensors remain in their existing builder closures.

With image input enabled under PP, the upstream tower context replaces
nonlocal vision/aligner modules with `StageMissingLayer`. These modules
are not `None`, so the previous loader still attempted to look up absent
local parameters and could raise `KeyError: aligner.w1.bias`. Skip only
disabled vision components or parameters belonging to a missing PP
tower; keep unknown local parameters as errors. This includes
LostFox11's commit `87ba8aae985254e916bbea5d0f45750a11351dbd`,
cherry-picked with attribution.

Fixes #22824.

Related: #20508.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Fixes an A5 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash startup failure exposed by reordered
metadata producers under PP2, while preserving submission-local
visible-length reuse. The dependency is on producer ordering, so it is
not inherently limited to PP configurations. Also fixes enabled-ViT PP
startup when checkpoint vision weights belong to another pipeline stage.

commits.message:
[Feature] Pick the quantized all-reduce min_numel default per TP on A2 (#22085)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The int8 quantized all-reduce added in #19000 is gated by a payload
threshold, `min_numel`, and ships with a single default of `16777216`
elements (32 MiB of bf16 payload). One number cannot fit all TP degrees:
the break-even payload is strongly TP-dependent, because the bf16 HCCS
bandwidth grows with the group size while the fixed cost of the int8
path (`absmax`, 8 KiB fp32 `amax` all-reduce, quantize, dequantize) does
not.

Measured on 910B3 (A2) with a dependent chain of 16 collectives — the
timing protocol that reproduces serving TTFT to within 1–5% — the
break-even payload is:

| TP | break-even (chained) | shipped default | this PR | payload | gain
at the gate | gain at the serving shape |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 9–11 MiB | 32 MiB | **8,388,608** | 16 MiB | 1.45x | 1.82x @160
MiB |
| 4 | 21–23 MiB | 32 MiB | **16,777,216** | 32 MiB | 1.30x | 1.59x @80
MiB |
| 8 | 31–38 MiB | 32 MiB | **31,457,280** | 60 MiB | 1.11x | 1.24x @160
MiB |

(`min_numel` is in elements; a bf16 payload of `N` elements is `N * 2`
bytes, so `N = MiB * 524,288`.)

The crossing is reproducible with a dependent chain: on an idle 8-card
910B3 node it reports 10.6 / 22.7 / 43.7 MiB for TP=2/4/8 and gains of
1.47x / 1.28x / 1.07x at the three defaults, with a second pass landing
at ~10 / ~21 / 41.4 MiB. A later 37-point rescan of TP=8 in 64-token
steps puts the chained crossing at 31–38 MiB (see **End-to-end results**
below); end to end, int8 is still neutral at 50 MiB and first pays at 60
MiB.

So the single 32 MiB default is ~1.5x above break-even at TP=2 and TP=4,
where it is simply conservative, but it undershoots TP=8's end-to-end
crossing: int8 is neutral at 50 MiB (+0.17% TTFT) and only turns
profitable at 60 MiB (−1.89%). That band is reached as soon as
`max_num_batched_tokens` is lowered or a smaller hidden size is served,
which is exactly when a bad gate costs throughput.

### End-to-end results with these gates

`vllm bench serve` against this branch on top of #19000: Qwen3.8-27B
(dense, hidden 5120, 64 layers, bf16) on 1 node × 8×910B3,
`--no-enable-prefix-caching`, `--max-concurrency 1`, 16 prompts, 256
output tokens, 2 warmups; each payload point is measured in 2 sweeps and
the tables report the median. The payload is pinned by construction: a
prefill chunk of `L` tokens issues `[L, 5120]` bf16 collectives, i.e. `L
× 10,240` bytes, so `payload (MiB) = L / 102.4`.

| TP | gate payload | bf16 TTFT | int8 TTFT | **Δ TTFT** | Δ p99 TTFT |
Δ at 160 MiB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 16.0 MiB (L=1639) | 396.1 | 360.5 | **−8.99%** | −7.17% | −12.79%
|
| 4 | 32.0 MiB (L=3277) | 439.3 | 409.6 | **−6.77%** | −7.03% | −9.27% |
| 8 | 60.0 MiB (L=6144) | 466.9 | 458.1 | **−1.89%** | −1.80% | −4.65% |

At payloads that are still too small the two arms are indistinguishable
(TP=8 21.5 MiB +0.10%, 43.0 +0.03%, 50.0 +0.17%; TP=4 22.0 −0.18%; TP=2
10.0 −0.58%), which is the ±0.6% noise floor of this setup. TPOT is flat
everywhere (max deviation 0.08 ms): a decode step moves 1 token, i.e.
5120 elements = 10 KiB, three orders of magnitude below the smallest
gate.

TP=8 is the only gate that is not ~1.5× above its crossing, so the whole
band was swept:

| payload | L | bf16 TTFT | int8 TTFT | Δ TTFT | Δ p99 TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 21.5 MiB | 2202 | 314.9 | 315.2 | +0.10% | +0.85% |
| 43.0 MiB | 4403 | 355.6 | 355.7 | +0.03% | +0.55% |
| 50.0 MiB | 5121 | 406.4 | 407.1 | +0.17% | +0.77% |
| **60.0 MiB** | 6144 | 466.9 | 458.1 | **−1.89%** | **−1.80%** |
| 80.0 MiB | 8192 | 604.1 | 595.2 | −1.48% | −1.19% |
| 100.0 MiB | 10240 | 749.0 | 732.5 | −2.20% | −2.26% |
| 160.0 MiB | 16384 | 1212.6 | 1156.2 | −4.65% | −5.57% |

The bf16 column is linear over the whole range (`TTFT ≈ 39 + 0.0717
ms/token`, seven points, residual ≤3.7%), and the bf16 anchors
re-measured in the 60/80/100 MiB session agree with the earlier session
within 0.2% at 21.5 / 43 / 50 / 160 MiB. **The end-to-end crossing sits
between 50 and 60 MiB**, which is why the TP=8 default is 60 MiB rather
than the 31–38 MiB collective crossing: a real forward keeps only 40–90%
of the isolated chain's gain.

A 37-point scan of the collective itself in 64-token steps (chained
protocol, 16 dependent collectives per window):

| payload | 40 | 45 | 50 | 60 | 80 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 | 0.698 ms | 0.770 | 0.858 | 0.990 | 1.300 |
| int8 | 0.691 | 0.727 | 0.784 | 0.891 | 1.124 |
| speedup | 1.01× | 1.06× | 1.09× | 1.11× | 1.16× |

bf16 is a straight line across the whole range (no message-size or
algorithm step); the chained crossing is 31–38 MiB (31 MiB fitting the
≥46 MiB region, 38 MiB from the 40/80 MiB endpoints). At 60 MiB the
chain promises 0.099 ms × 128 collectives = 12.7 ms against 8.8 ms
measured end to end.

The gate fires only where intended: with `min_numel=31457280` the
activation log shows `(6144,5120)` ×32, `(8192,5120)` ×32 and
`(10240,5120)` ×48, and no `(2202,5120)` / `(4403,5120)` /
`(5121,5120)`. `(16384,5120)` is the graph-capture dummy pass at
start-up. `total_input_tokens = 16 × L` in every result JSON confirms no
length jitter, and no doubled-length shape appears, so two requests
never merged into one chunk.

Accuracy is unaffected: GPQA-diamond (198 questions,
`max_out_len=130000`, no MTP) shows no significant delta at any TP —
TP=8 +1.52 pp (pooled p=0.52), TP=4 +0.25 pp (p=1.00), TP=2 −1.01 pp
(p=0.64).

What changes:

- `QuantizedAllReduceConfig.min_numel` becomes `int | None = None`.
`None` means "pick the measured default of the selected backend"; an
explicit value still wins and is still validated (`>= 1`).
- The int8 default is resolved in `QuantizedAllReduce.__init__` rather
than in the config object, because that is the first place where both
the real group size and the device check are known
(`_validate_preconditions` only sees `tensor_parallel_size`, and the
config is frozen).
- New `_DEFAULT_MIN_NUMEL_A2` / `default_min_numel(world_size,
device_type)`: 8,388,608 (16 MiB) at TP=2, 16,777,216 (32 MiB) at TP=4,
31,457,280 (60 MiB) at TP=8. The table is A2-only: an A5 int8
configuration that leaves `min_numel` at `null` is rejected at config
time, because A5 has no int8 payload calibration and reusing the A2
gates there could enable the path below its own crossing. On A2, degrees
that were not measured (3, 5–7) take the next larger entry, so the gate
never undercuts a measured break-even; groups larger than 8 ranks keep
bf16 as before.
- The MXFP8 backend that landed in #21508 has no per-TP calibration, so
it resolves `None` to its own `_DEFAULT_MIN_NUMEL = 16,777,216` (32
MiB). `min_numel` therefore keeps one meaning on both backends — "`None`
= the backend's measured default" — without inventing A5 numbers here.
- The start-up log prints the group and the resolved gate (`INT8
quantized all-reduce enabled (group=..., min_numel=..., max_q=...)`),
since that value is group-dependent.
- `distributed/device_communicators/quantized_all_reduce.py` is renamed
to `int8_all_reduce.py`: it only implements the int8 backend, while
MXFP8 lives in `mxfp8_all_reduce.py`. The config key and the backend
selection are unchanged.

> **Rebased onto `main` after #21508 landed.** Both PRs edit
`ascend_config.py`, the int8 all-reduce module and
`npu_communicator.py`; the resolution keeps #21508's `quant_dtype`
selection and MXFP8 routing intact and only splits the threshold by
backend: int8 uses the per-TP table below, MXFP8 keeps 32 MiB.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, a configuration default:
`additional_config.quantized_all_reduce_config.min_numel` now defaults
to `null` instead of `16777216`, and `AscendConfig.unified_json` reports
`"min_numel": null`. On the int8 backend `null` means "the measured gate
for this TP degree"; on MXFP8 it means 32 MiB as before, so A5
deployments on the default backend see no change. If the int8 backend is
forced on A5, `min_numel` must be set explicitly, since the per-TP table
is calibrated on A2 only. Existing configs that set `min_numel`
explicitly are unaffected, and the feature is still opt-in via `enable`.
A release note fragment is added.

### How was this patch tested?

Unit tests on 8x910B3 (CANN 9.2.1, torch_npu 2.10.0):

- `tests/ut/distributed/device_communicators/test_int8_all_reduce.py` →
23 passed, including four new cases: per-TP defaults (2/4/8), "the
per-TP defaults resolve on A2 only" (an A5 wrapper without an explicit
value raises), "an unmeasured TP never resolves below a measured
break-even" (3 → TP=4 entry, 5/6/7 → TP=8 entry), and "an explicit
`min_numel` wins over the default".
- `tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py -k QuantizedAllReduce` → 13 passed,
including the new `min_numel=None` case, the A5-without-`min_numel`
rejection, and the backend-default cases from #21508.
- `tests/ut/distributed/device_communicators/test_mxfp8_all_reduce.py` →
7 passed (untouched by the semantics change, re-run because
`Mxfp8AllReduce` now accepts `None`).
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on all touched Python
files.
- End-to-end `vllm bench serve` for every gate payload, plus the TP=8
payload sweep, the 37-point collective scan and the activation-log check
— all numbers are in **End-to-end results** above. Timings are only
meaningful on an idle node: with a co-tenant job on one card the same
sweep reported 3.4 ms instead of 2.6 ms for bf16 at 160 MiB and produced
no crossing at all.

The local container ships an older vllm than current `main`, so the full
`tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py` cannot run unmodified here: 72 tests
fail on the missing
`CompilationConfig.prefill_cudagraph_capture_token_sizes`. To make sure
that is not caused by this change, I ran the same file on a clean
`origin/main` checkout: 98 passed + the same 72 failures, versus 101
passed + the same 72 failures here. The change adds three passing tests
and no failure.

The dependent-chain convention was validated against end-to-end serving
in #19000 (chained predicts −2.09 s at TP=2 / 8K against −2.07 s
measured; the single-call convention predicts −1.87 s). This PR does not
touch the data path — it only moves the dispatch threshold — so the
gates were re-derived from those sweeps and then confirmed end to end
above.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: new tests cover
`min_numel=None`, an explicit value that differs from the default, and
unmeasured TP degrees (3, 5–7).
- [ ] **Regression test**: not a bug fix; the existing wrapper tests
already pin the int8/bf16 dispatch boundary.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: unchanged, the existing
`min_numel` validator tests still cover `0` and negative values.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: the new tests assert the resolved
gate behaviour, not just that construction succeeds.
- [x] **Performance impact**: end-to-end data above — −8.99% / −6.77% /
−1.89% TTFT at the three gates, −12.79% / −9.27% / −4.65% at 160 MiB;
every default now sits at or above its measured crossing.

Use `<planner_port>` from the planner command to show which values to

guide and the RFork parser. An explicit JSON boolean takes precedence,
an absent key enables environment fallback, and any other JSON type
causes initialization to fail.

No. This change updates the RFork guide and its Chinese translation.

### How was this patch tested?

tools/rtd_build.sh` in strict mode and verified the placeholder and
configuration row in both rendered RFork pages.

passed) and validated the Chinese catalog with `msgfmt --check`.

---

involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or

commits.message:
[BugFix][MoE] Share the MegaMoE buffer for DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark on A5 (#23017)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with DSpark can have 384 routed experts and top-k 6
in the target, and 128 experts and top-k 3 in the draft. The different
expert counts create distinct FUSED_MC2 communication objects. On Atlas
A5, creating two CANN MegaMoE buffers on the same communicator and op
tag can leave the second context with invalid peer addresses during
startup profiling. This PR follows up on #21727 and its revert #22964.

After the MRv2 DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark loader returns, it attempts sharing
only when the draft executes MoE, the hardware supports the A5 CANN MXFP
channel, MegaMoE is enabled and FUSED_MC2 is selected. A target and
draft with different expert counts can share if they execute serially,
use the same supported routed quantization and hidden width, have
compatible communication parameters, and the draft fits the target
buffer. The participating ranks must agree.

On CANN r148 the target and draft can use different expert counts on the
same communicator and op tag when they run serially, their communication
attributes match, and the draft fits the target allocation. The target
owns the allocation. The draft view retains that context and supplies
its own expert count and top-k.

After the layout checks, all ranks compare the draft's requirements with
the actual target allocation using the installed CANN size query. If the
target owns a buffer on this group and any rank rejects sharing, model
loading fails before the draft can allocate a second buffer on the same
tag.

Across sleep/wake, the shared buffer preserves the captured context
address. If the CANN factory raises on any rank, all ranks require a
fresh MC2 group before retrying because CANN may already have registered
the tag. Failures after a successful allocation can retry over that
allocation.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Eligible target/draft pairs on A5 reuse one MegaMoE buffer. Equal expert
counts and layouts rejected by the initial eligibility checks follow
their existing initialization paths. A final compatibility check that
fails after the current group has been claimed reports a startup error.
A3 skips the sharing check at the hardware gate. Relative to the PR
base, the quantization modules, the unquantized MoE weight path, and the
platform communication selector are unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

#### CPU regression tests

The following runs cover earlier revisions of this PR.

| Source and test coverage | Result |
| --- | --- |
| #23017 focused suite with the repository's vLLM pin (`c410543d9`) |
732 passed |
| #23017 focused suite with the image's vLLM (`4ba787ec9`) | 725 passed,
7 skipped |
| #23017 and #21830 together with the repository's vLLM pin | 1069
passed |
| #23017 and #21830 together with the image's vLLM, rerun after the
test-file rename in 112's `lhf_r148` | 1062 passed, 7 skipped |

The core cases are in `tests/ut/ops/test_dspark_mega_moe_buffer.py`.
They cover a compatible 384/128 pair, equal expert counts, A3 and A5
hardware profiles, W4A8 target with an unquantized draft, existing draft
buffers, capacity checks, rank disagreement, and sleep/wake. The
incompatible-quantization cases verify that the existing buffers and
transport registry entries retain their identities. The wider suite
covers MoE, quantization, model loading, graph configuration, and other
model paths. A two-process CPU Gloo test exercised rank-local release
failure and collective retry with a simulated allocator.

On the review revision, three new regression cases failed against the
previous implementation and passed with the fix. They cover a local
capacity veto, a peer capacity veto, and a factory failure after tag
registration. The 12-file suite passed all 596 tests against the
repository's paired vLLM (`c410543d9`). A two-rank Gloo test injected
factory errors on one rank and on both ranks, verified that no rank
reallocated on the failed group, and recovered on a fresh group. CANN
allocation failures were simulated in this test.

#### A5 hardware validation

The two earlier runs used DeepSeek V4.1 Flash W4A8MXFP with five-token
DSpark, the CANN 9.3.0 r148 image (`9722b0304456`), and #23017 together
with #21830. MegaMoE was explicitly enabled with `enable_fused_mc2=2`.

- **1P1D on 107 and 108.** All eight Prefill ranks shared the target's
MegaMoE context with the draft and submitted the CANN MegaMoE kernel for
both models. Short, long, and decode requests returned HTTP 200, with
the same text and token IDs as the `dispatch_ffn_combine` baseline. A
separate fresh 2493-token prompt exercised Mooncake KV transfer and
produced 32 output tokens. The MegaMoE run recorded 33 draft proposals
and 80 accepted tokens.
- **Colocated Prefill and Decode on 112 in `lhf_r148`.** DP8/TP1/EP8
started with `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`. All eight ranks confirmed that the
384-expert/top-6 target and 128-expert/top-3 draft had the same context,
device address, and buffer owner. All 22 requests returned HTTP 200,
including 11 long prompts of 2492 tokens. After the initial pair, four
serial calls and two eight-way concurrent rounds exercised all eight DP
ranks. The repeated rounds added 136 draft proposals and 218 accepted
tokens. All responses contained the expected answer. In 15 of 20
repeated calls, generated token IDs matched the corresponding initial
response. Five concurrent long responses differed in tokens after the
correct answer. The health check still returned HTTP 200 after the last
round.

**Review revision on A5 with EPLB enabled.** The Prefill and Decode
roles ran separately on the same eight A5 devices with the openEuler
CANN 9.3.0 r148 image (`9bd8129dbc44`), the reviewed MegaMoE changes and
#21830 on the image's vLLM-Ascend base. Both used DP8/TP1/EP8, W4A8MXFP,
five-token DSpark, `enable_fused_mc2=3`, and EPLB with 16 redundant
target experts. On all eight ranks in both roles, the 400-expert/top-6
target and 128-expert/top-3 draft shared the same context object, device
address and buffer owner.

- **Prefill, eager.** Six requests sent directly to the producer
returned HTTP 200 and generated 1, 1, 1, 8, 16 and 32 tokens.
Speculative decoding counters recorded 130 proposed tokens and 29
accepted tokens.
- **Decode, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`.** All eight API ranks became ready.
Graph capture completed for all 41 target and 37 draft sizes.

Native HCCL sleep/wake, formal accuracy evaluation, and throughput
benchmarking remain open.

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] Boundary and edge cases for expert counts, quantization, topology
and buffer capacity
- [x] Regression cases for sharing and for preserving native behavior
when sharing is skipped
- [x] Failure-path coverage for rank disagreement and buffer recovery
- [x] Tests assert buffer identity, registered method identity and
captured addresses
- [ ] A5 performance benchmarks

[CI] Add /download command and delegate model cache downloads to sync-tools (#21934)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

NPU E2E tests can only run a model once it is on the cluster disk, and
the download itself is network-bound. Today the downloads run in-job on
business O-card NPU runners (`linux-aarch64-a2b3-0`, `a3-800t-0`,
`a3-800i-2`, `a5-0`),
which holds NPU nodes for TB-scale pulls, and `cancel-in-progress: true`
can interrupt a download mid-blob and leave a truncated cache.

This PR moves the download off the Ascend runners entirely and delegates
it to the `ascend-gha-runners/sync-tools` model-library pipeline, and
adds a maintainer `/download` command so the caches can be populated
without a
same-repo PR branch.

- Renames `labeled_download_model_dataset.yaml` to
`pr_download_command.yml` with three triggers:
- `pull_request` on the `model-dataset-download` label (unchanged
behavior);
- `repository_dispatch` via a new `/download` slash command (triage+, PR
comments only), which also works for fork PRs where the label-triggered
run cannot read repository secrets;
- `workflow_dispatch` with explicit `models`/`datasets`/`cluster` inputs
for repairing a cache whose ledger drifted from
`model_dataset_list.json`.
- Uses a single CPU runner (`linux-amd64-cpu-1-hk`) instead of one
Ascend runner per cluster.
- Diffs `model_dataset_list.json` (PR head vs `main`) per cluster and
request only the clusters that actually receive something. `a3` and
`a3-560t` are separate targets; `models.310p` travels with the `a3`
volume the 310p tests mount.
- The triggering comment reports progress in place (accepted →
per-cluste status with the sync-tools job link → final summary), with a
3h wait budget; already-cached items return in seconds (idempotent).
- Registers the command in `slash_command_dispatch.yml`, documents it in
`docs/source/community/slash-commands.md` (and its zh_CN `.po`), and
lists `linux-amd64-cpu-1-hk` in `.github/actionlint.yaml`.

One-time prerequisite for maintainers: a fine-grained PAT scoped to
`ascend-gha-runners/sync-tools` (Actions: read/write), stored as the
`MODEL_SYNC_PAT` repo/org secret.

No behavior change for forks/PRs without the `model-dataset-download`
label.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No — this is a CI/workflow and documentation-only change. The new
`/download` command is a maintainer-facing CI tool, not an end-user API
or runtime behavior change, so no release-note fragment is added.

### How was this patch tested?

- YAML syntax and `actionlint` for `pr_download_command.yml`,
`slash_command_dispatch.yml` and `.github/actionlint.yaml`.
- <TODO: manual `workflow_dispatch` run against a test cluster / a
label-triggered run on a same-repo PR — attach the run link and the
  per-cluster comment output>.
- <TODO: docs build for `slash-commands.md` and the zh_CN `.po` (e.g.
`make docs` /
  translation check)>.

commits.message:
[BugFix][310P] Keep default preferred block size at 128 (#23174)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix a 310P paged decode performance regression on
`Qwen3-32B-w8a8sc-310p` nightly CI (e.g., [run 45481439104 / job
138756093908](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45481439104/job/138756093908))
introduced after upgrading vLLM from `v0.33.0` to `v0.34.0` (#22198).

#### Root Cause

- Upstream vLLM PR `#63231` (`[Core] Change default --block-size from 16
to 64`) changed `CacheConfig.DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE` from `16` to `64`.
- In `vllm_ascend/_310p/attention/attention_v1.py`,
`AscendAttentionBackend310.get_preferred_block_size(default_block_size)`
checked `if cls.supports_block_size(default_block_size): return
default_block_size` before falling back to `128`.
- With `DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE=16` (`v0.33.0`), `supports_block_size(16)`
returned `False` and fell back to `128`.
- With `DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE=64` (`v0.34.0`), `supports_block_size(64)`
returned `True` (since `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()` is `[128,
64]`), silently downgrading the resolved 310P KV cache `block_size` from
`128` to `64` even when `--block-size` was not specified by the user.
- On 310P (`Qwen3-32B-w8a8sc-310-vllm-tp4`, `bs=8`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`),
halving `block_size` from `128` to `64` doubled the block table width
(`(32, 160)` -> `(32, 320)`) and increased
`paged_attention_decoder_mask_0` kernel latency by +34.6% (`77.66 us` ->
`104.55 us` per layer, `+1.72 ms/step` across 64 layers), pushing output
throughput below the CI threshold (`99.67 < 0.95 * 105.26 = 99.997
token/s`).

#### Fix

- Return `128` directly in
`AscendAttentionBackend310.get_preferred_block_size()` (matching
upstream's ROCm fix in vLLM `#63231`).
- Explicit `--block-size 64` runs bypass `get_preferred_block_size()`
and continue to work via `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes() == [128,
64]`.
- Add unit test
`TestAscendAttentionBackend310.test_get_preferred_block_size` covering
default block sizes `16`, `64`, and `128`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This restores the intended 310P default KV cache block size (`128`)
without changing CLI flags or explicit `--block-size` behavior.

### How was this patch tested?

1. **Unit test** (on Ascend 310P container, `Python 3.12.13`, `vllm
0.34.0`):
   ```bash
pytest --noconftest -v tests/ut/_310p/attention/test_attention_v1_310.py
-k TestAscendAttentionBackend310
   # 4 passed (including test_get_preferred_block_size)
   ```
2. **Static checks**:
   - `ruff check` & `ruff format --check` passed on both changed files.
   - `git diff --check` passed.
3. **310P Hardware Verification** (`Atlas 300I Duo / 310P3`, TP=4, CANN
`9.3.0 / V100R001C13B060`, `torch_npu 2.10.0.post7`,
`Qwen3-32B-w8a8sc-310-vllm-tp4`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`,
`cudagraph_capture_sizes=[8,32]`, `bs=8`, ~512 input tokens):
- Verified KV cache & block table shapes restored from `(2871, 16, 64,
16)` / `(32, 320)` back to `(1436, 16, 128, 16)` / `(32, 160)`.
   - Benchmark comparison on the same 4 NPUs:

| Version | Workload (`bs=8`, ~512 in) | Avg TTFT | Avg TPOT | Output
Throughput |
   |---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `v0.33.0` (`4ba787ec` + `66f6ef21`) | 256 out | 1974.22 ms | 72.77 ms
| 99.40 token/s |
| `v0.34.0` (`62d4bc3c` + `9b8c54e0`, before fix) | 256 out | 2015.34 ms
| 75.02 ms | 96.55 token/s |
| **`v0.34.0` + this PR** | **256 out** | **1993.57 ms** | **73.06 ms**
| **98.96 token/s** |
| **`v0.34.0` + this PR** | **512 out (CI parity)** | **2019.36 ms** |
**72.41 ms** | **104.79 token/s** |

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: Covered default block sizes
`16`, `64`, and `128` and verified `supports_block_size(64)` /
`supports_block_size(128)` remain `True`.
- [x] **Regression test**: Added `test_get_preferred_block_size` which
fails without this fix when `default_block_size=64`.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: N/A (single constant preference
return; unsupported explicit block sizes remain validated by existing
`supports_block_size` checks).
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New test directly asserts backend
block size preference and support contract.
- [x] **Performance impact**: Attached 310P TP=4 before/after benchmark
and profiling results confirming full recovery of
`Qwen3-32B-w8a8sc-310p` decode throughput.

commits.message:
[Feature] Support mrope_section [8, 12, 12] in fused MRoPE (#22935)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

#3708 introduced the fused MRoPE operator but only whitelisted
`mrope_section == [16, 24, 24]` (validated for Qwen2.5-VL at the time).
MinerU2.5-Pro-2605-1.2B (Qwen2-VL) uses `mrope_section: [8, 12, 12]`, so
it silently fell back to the decomposed base-class implementation.

On MinerU2.5-Pro-2605-1.2B (single Ascend 910B3, 20 concurrency, one
1024x1024 image per request) that fallback produced 25,735 `Mul`, 25,728
`Mul_Slice`, 19,744 `Cat_Slice`, 13,548 `ConcatD`, and 3,504`Index`
kernels per profiled run - roughly 97k extra small kernels.

This PR extends the whitelist to `[8, 12, 12]` so it takes
`torch_npu.npu_mrope`. The numerical semantics are unchanged: the same
`rotary_mode="half"` and the same section split are passed to the
operator, and 1D positions still degrade to `mrope_section=[0, 0, 0]`
(standard RoPE mode). Other sections keep the base-class fallback.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Models configured with `mrope_section: [8, 12, 12]` (e.g. MinerU2.5) now
use the fused `npu_mrope` operator instead of the decomposed fallback.
No new API, CLI option, or environment variable; sections other than
`[16, 24, 24]` and `[8, 12, 12]` are unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

```bash
pytest -q tests/ut/ops/test_rotary_embedding.py
```

Added UTs assert that `[8, 12, 12]` reaches `torch_npu.npu_mrope` with
the expected section and `rotary_mode="half"`, that 1D positions degrade
to `mrope_section=[0, 0, 0]`, that the cos/sin cache follows the query
dtype, and that the existing `[16, 24, 24]` and fallback paths are
unchanged. rope-related UT files: 116 passed, verified against the
CI-pinned vLLM main commit c410543d9fff.

Same-load comparison on MinerU2.5-Pro-2605-1.2B (single Ascend 910B3, 20
concurrency, one 1024x1024 image per request, 256 input / 128 output
tokens, temperature=0, seed=42, ignore_eos), before vs after with the
torch profiler，In single-layer computation, all small operators are
replaced by the fused RopeWithSinCosCache operator. The latency is
reduced from 112 us to 14 us, achieving a 0.1 ms improvement per layer.

Accuracy: the three changes of this series (KV cache layout, mrope
section [8, 12, 12], fused vision QKV+RoPE) were validated together on
MinerU2.5-Pro-2605-1.2B; the end-to-end OmniDocBench score moved from
94.23 to 94.14, within run-to-run variance.

[BugFix] Keep Qwen QSA tiling buffers stable for padded decode graphs (#23192)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix stale QSA tiling metadata when MRV2 replays a non-PCP full decode
graph with fewer live rows than the captured shape. For example, with
three MTP draft tokens, 15 requests use 60 rows and replay the graph
captured for 64. The QSA input adapter introduced in #21634 keys its

padding rows remain unmapped.

[Refactor][WeightTransfer] Reuse vLLM packed loops and shared unpacking (#20676)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Reuse vLLM's packed HCCL producer and consumer loops, including packing,
cached slot streams, rotation and normal-path drains. Keep Ascend's
native HCCL stream dispatch/ordering, failure cleanup and fixed-buffer
NPU IPC implementation. Reuse upstream `PackedIpcChunk` while preserving
the IPC RPC payload.

The local consumer adapter preserves independent storage and unaligned
mixed dtypes. It orders callbacks across slots and tracks cloned storage
on the slot/caller streams. A loader's `StopIteration` propagates as an
error instead of triggering an extra receive. Additional reader streams
remain responsible for their own readiness and storage tracking.

Packed HCCL calls on the same process/device must run serially on every
rank. A process-local device guard rejects overlapping calls before the
second collective and remains active through cleanup. This is fail-fast
serialization, not concurrent communicator isolation. Stream-cache
compatibility checks remain local to the adapter. NPU execution uses the
existing shared CUDA API wrapper in NPU-only processes; its replacements
are process-wide.

### Does this PR introduce any user facing change?

Yes. Retained weights are protected across packed HCCL slot callbacks.
Overlapping packed HCCL calls on the same process/device raise
`RuntimeError`; finish an update on every rank before starting the next.

### How was this patch tested?

interface adaptations and regressions for loader exceptions, stream
draining, overlap rejection/recovery and compatibility failures. Only

[Feature][PCP] Align short-prefill dispatch across attention backends (#21688)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

When a request has an existing computed prefix and only one new prompt
token to process, it can still be in the prefill lifecycle. Under PCP,
partitioning that request as prefill while attention runs it as decode
can make request ownership, graph dispatch, and attention metadata
disagree.

This PR classifies eligible one-token prompt tails as decode work before
PCP graph dispatch. The classification excludes speculative draft tokens
and applies when `PCP > 1`, `DCP == 1`, and decode-request sharding is
enabled.

- Preserves the original lifecycle flags for prompt preparation and
sampling. Dispatch, partitioning, and attention metadata apply the same
explicit host masks through `apply_prefill_as_decode_mask`.
- Returns the original batch when no request qualifies. For batches with
an override, the runner publishes the dispatch mask after FlashMLA
finalizes request order, so dispatch sizing and graph eligibility use
the same request layout as partitioning.
- Makes FlashMLA consume the effective phase directly from attention
metadata. MLA honors that phase under PCP, so a genuine prefill fragment
stays on the prefill path even when its rank-local query has one token.
- Uses the same effective phase for DeepSeek V4.1 C2 compressor sends
and ring updates. Request ownership and slot mapping reuse the paired
vLLM PCP implementation.
- Extends CPU regression coverage for indirect FLA imports through Kimi
during model discovery.

Related upstream work adds shared handling for cached one-token prefills
in vLLM, including classification, graph dispatch, and PCP partitioning.
Once that change is available in the vLLM versions supported by Ascend,
we can reuse the upstream implementation and simplify the Ascend-side
batch handling. [vLLM
#69512](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69512)

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. With PCP decode-request sharding enabled, eligible one-token prompt
tails follow decode request ownership and can use compatible decode
graphs. Existing deployments pick up this routing behavior with their
current configuration.

### How was this patch tested?

both the failed run's base and the current `main`. The rebased tree

commits.message:
[Feature][Quantization] Support HiF8 C8 KV cache for sparse-attention MLA (#22750)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

related RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/23078

Adds HIF8 (HiFloat8) C8 KV cache quantization for the NoPE
sparse-attention MLA layers of GLM-5.3-Flash (glm5next) on Ascend 950
(A5), driven by ModelSlim `QK_HIF8_PER_TENSOR` layer recipes and enabled
via `--kv-cache-dtype hif8`. HIF8 stores each latent element as one byte
(vs. two for BF16), halving the NoPE KV footprint and extending the
usable context capacity on A5.

Key changes:

- **KV cache registration**: registers the `hif8` cache dtype as a uint8
latent payload whose NoPE page layout is identical to BF16 — no
repacking and no per-token scales embedded in the cache, so P2P KV
transfer treats HIF8 pages as opaque buffers. Only layers exported with
the recipe are quantized; all other layers (RoPE attention, draft/MTP
paths) keep the model dtype.
- **Per-layer HIF8 KV method**
(`vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/kv_cache/hif8_c8.py`):
loads the static `fa_q`/`fa_k` per-tensor scales from the
checkpoint(uniform per-layer vectors are accepted; non-uniform exports
are rejected at
startup with a clear message). Q and latent KV are quantized per-tensor
and attention runs on `aclnnQuantSparseFlashMla` from the CANN toolkit.
- **Sparse MLA attention path** (`sfa_v1.py`): `sparse_mla` takes an
optional
`hif8_scales` argument; when present, the query is quantized via
`torch_npu.npu_quantize` (HIFLOAT8 raw uint8 = cache storage format) and
dispatches to `quant_sparse_flash_mla` with
`q_descale`/`ori_kv_descale`. The SMLA plan builder selects the
quantized metadata operator accordingly.
- **SMLA metadata size correctness**: `SMLA_METADATA_SIZE` is now
mirrored at
runtime from the installed `cann_ops_transformer` package instead of
using a hardcoded constant — CANN 9.2 operators allocate a 1024-int32
plan while CANN 9.3 grew it to 2048, and the persistent buffer must
match the operator that fills it. The historical 1024 is kept only as a
fallback for environments where the package is absent.
- **ModelSlim recipe handling**: a recipe containing HIF8 quant types
now
disables the legacy FAKQuant `fa_quant` route, whose TP-sharded scale
loader cannot consume per-tensor exports. The weights mapper drops the
`fa_v` / offset suffixes only for the `hif8` dtype; other dtypes keep
dropping the whole family, so pure FAKQuant / MXFP checkpoints are
unaffected.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. A new `--kv-cache-dtype hif8` option is available for GLM-5.3-Flash
on A5, quantizing exactly the layers exported with the ModelSlim
`QK_HIF8_PER_TENSOR` recipe (see the included release note fragment).
Existing dtypes (`auto`/`fp8`) and non-GLM models are unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

commits.message:
[BugFix][Sleep Mode] Fix SIGABRT when CaMem memory is freed while asleep (#23137)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Split out of #22865 to keep that PR to RFC #22572 P3, as suggested in
review. First reported in #20528.

Refs #22572

Sleep unmaps each CaMem allocation and frees its physical memory, but
kept the handle. A tensor freed while its allocation is asleep then
reaches `my_free`, which calls `unmap_and_release` on the same handle
again. `aclrtUnmapMem` fails with ACL error 507899, and because the C++
exception escapes the Python binding, the process aborts (SIGABRT). This
happens whenever a sleeping engine shuts down, and, once `discard` is
supported (#22865), when an engine shuts down after
`release_kv_cache_memory()` without waking the KV cache.

`unmap_and_release` now clears the handle once the physical memory is
freed and returns early for a cleared handle, so `my_free` only releases
the address. `create_and_map` writes a new handle on wake-up, so wake-up
is unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Shutting down an engine whose memory is asleep no longer aborts the
process. Fragment: `release_notes/fragments/23137.yaml`.

### How was this patch tested?

A3, Qwen3-0.6B, vLLM `c410543d9` and v0.33.0, comparing the image's
`vllm_ascend_C` with one rebuilt with this change (measured on #22865's
branch, which includes the same change):

| Case | Without the fix | With the fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free a weights tensor during sleep, then release the pool |
`aclrtUnmapMem failed with acl error code: 507899`, exit 134 | exit 0 |
| Shut down awake | clean | clean |
| Shut down after `sleep(1)` | EngineCore exit code -6 (SIGABRT) | no
abort |
| Shut down after `release_kv_cache_memory()`, KV not woken | EngineCore
exit code -6 (SIGABRT) | no abort |

With the rebuilt library, two level-1 and two staged level-2 sleep/wake
cycles keep identical greedy output, so wake-up still maps a new handle
into the cleared slot. The NPU CaMem UT (`tests/ut/device_allocator/`)
passes on both lanes (19 passed).

There is no CPU UT for this path: it is C++ and needs the NPU runtime.

[BugFix][KV Pool] Fix layerwise callback indexing for shared KV under pipeline parallelism (#22394)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

A shared-source KV cache can register cache views for a layer that runs
on an earlier pipeline stage. For example, with a 24+16 split of
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, stage 1 holds a mirror of layer 20 and runs decoder
layers 24 through 39. The layerwise worker receives 16 forward hooks on
that stage. Counting model-wide layer IDs or giving the mirror its own
hook can leave the final save wait scheduled after the last forward
hook.

Use the local stage bounds when registering shared-source cache views.
Associate incoming mirrors with the first local hook so their historical
prefix rows are available there. The last executing layer reaches the
existing final-save wait. PP1 and the fallback for older layer-index
APIs retain their previous behavior. The change is confined to the KV
pool. It introduces no model-specific layer IDs or prefetch settings.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. With shared-source models and producer-side pipeline parallelism,
layerwise Memcache transfers now follow the actual layer execution order
and finish at the final local layer.

### How was this patch tested?

- Ran `python3 -m pytest -q tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store` on the
standalone patch. 1058 passed and 12 skipped. The new regression fails
against the unpatched base (40 callback slots for 20 local layers).
- Added unit coverage for 20+20, 24+16, and 14+26. It checks the HBM
buffer addresses scheduled by the first load, the full request's
transfer targets, and one final-save wait at the last local hook. A
separate in-memory byte round trip in the integrated build also checked
imported prefix content after the first wait, including a split where an
incoming source and a local source share that hook.
- Tested on Ascend A5 using DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, eager Model Runner V2,
a PP2/TP1/DCP1 producer with MooncakeConnectorV2 layerwise push and
Memcache layerwise pooling, and a PP1/TP1/DCP1 decoder. For each PP
partition, AISBench sent four cold and four warm prompts of 131072
tokens, with one greedy output token and concurrency 1. All 16 responses
matched the same inputs on the PP1 baseline. The second stage reported
20 and 16 callbacks, respectively, across all four producer DP ranks.
- The integration used the model support from #19284, its [A5 packed-row
scatter
fix](https://github.com/real-CLiang/vllm-ascend/commit/1028b45ba3be4e1bc2ea3ef7ae797f9dabb135eb),
and the GVA allocation/byte-offset changes in #20856. These are separate
changes with their own review scope.

| Producer PP partition | Cold mean P prefill | Warm mean P prefill | P
external hit tokens, cold / warm |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 20+20 | 13.488 s | 0.944 s | 0 / 523,776 |
| 24+16 | 15.740 s | 2.859 s | 0 / 523,776 |

**Concurrent cold/warm validation (Nov 20).** On the same Ascend A5
setup with the 24+16 producer partition, each request had 131,072 input
tokens. We routed one cold request and six warm requests to the same
producer DP rank. Two of the cold request’s Memcache writes overlapped
warm reads in the same worker, as measured around host-side `batch_copy`
calls. The longest overlap was 4.07 ms. The proxy received the cold
request’s prefill response about 210 ms after its last observed write
returned. All seven one-token outputs matched their serial references.
Replaying the cold prefix hit 130,944 external cache tokens and matched
a fresh cold reference. A separate concurrent cold/warm pair generated
eight tokens per request, and both sequences matched their serial
references.
