commits.message:
[Performance][PCP] Overlap local Q projection with global cache preparation (#21414)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DSA PCP prefill currently runs three things serially per layer:
gather/restore the hidden states, prepare the replicated caches (global
collectives), and only then compute the local Q prolog. The Q prolog
only reads local inputs and weights, so it can be issued on the
auxiliary stream while the caller stream performs the unchanged
collectives, hiding the Q cost behind communication.

This PR enables that overlap for PCP prefill on the existing DSA
multistream switch. No new configuration option is added:

- `_prepare_caches_and_query` replaces
`_prepare_caches_before_attention`: it prepares the caches and
optionally returns the Q intermediates produced by this invocation. The
base `AscendDSAImpl` implementation returns `(False, None)`, so non-PCP
behavior is untouched.
- `AscendDSAPCPImpl.__init__` maps the inherited
`multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap` value into `pcp_q_projection_overlap` and
then sets the inherited flag to `False`, because PCP has already
prepared the replicated caches before local attention and must not start
a second cache-update overlap on the base path.
- `AscendDSAPCPImpl._prepare_caches_and_query` issues
`_mla_prolog_single_stream` on the existing overlap stream
(`dsv4_dsa_overlap_stream()`) for layers whose PCP metadata has a global
prefill and whose local query shard is nonempty. Every collective stays
on the caller stream in its original order, empty local shards still
join all collectives and skip the Q prolog, and the Q stream is joined
in a `finally` block so a failure cannot leave an unsynchronized stream.
- `AscendDSAImpl.forward` / `_forward_attention` consume the
invocation-local `prepared_query` instead of recomputing the prolog;
nothing is cached on the layer.
- Unit tests in `tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_cp.py` and
`tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_v1.py` cover the config mapping, the
collective/stream ordering, and the failure-path join.

Serving behavior changes for PCP prefill: the overlap is on whenever
`multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap` is enabled, which is the documented
default (`True`).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, but there is no new switch: PCP prefill Q-projection overlap is
controlled by the pre-existing `multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap`
`additional-config` option (`vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py`, default
`True`). A PCP deployment therefore gets the overlap without any extra
flag, and `--additional-config '{"multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap":
false}'` restores the serial gather-then-Q order.

Docs and release notes shipped in this PR:

- `docs/source/user_guide/configuration/additional_config.md`: the
`multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap` row now also documents the PCP prefill
behavior and how to turn it off.
- `release_notes/fragments/21414.yaml`:

```yaml
pr: 21414
entries:
  - category: performance
    text: >-
      PCP prefill now overlaps the local Q projection with global cache
      preparation for nonempty local query shards, controlled by the existing
      `multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap` option (enabled by default). To run the
      two steps serially, launch with
      `--additional-config '{"multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap": false}'`.
```

### How was this patch tested?

#### 1. Unit tests (added in this PR)

`tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_cp.py` (+133) and
`tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_v1.py` (+20/-9) mock the NPU stream and
operator calls, so they need no NPU:

- `test_pcp_query_overlap_honors_config[False/True]`: `AscendDSAPCPImpl`
maps the inherited `multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap` value into
`pcp_q_projection_overlap` and leaves the inherited cache-update overlap
disabled.
- `test_cache_query_preparation_preserves_collectives` (12 cases:
overlap on/off x global-prefill/local-tokens x `compress_ratio`
1/4/128): asserts the Q prolog runs on the overlap stream only when
overlap is enabled, a global prefill exists and the local shard is
nonempty; the recorded call order is `query_wait, query, gather, swa[,
compressor][, indexer], weights, current_wait` for the overlapped cases
and the plain collective order otherwise, with no stream access at all
when overlap is off.
- `test_cache_query_preparation_joins_stream_on_failure` (7 injected
failure stages): the Q stream is still joined and the join is the last
stream operation.
- `test_cache_query_preparation_delegates_ordinary_metadata`: non-PCP
metadata falls back to the base implementation without touching any
stream or collective.
- `tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_v1.py`: `_make_impl`/`_forward_attention`
call sites are updated for the new `prepared_query` plumbing, including
the `prepared_query`-first branch that skips `_mla_prolog_multistream`.

#### 2. NPU microbenchmark (8x Ascend 910B3, TP1 + PCP8)

Measured with an out-of-tree harness during development of this PR (the
comparison script itself is not part of the final diff; raw records live
outside the repo). Synthetic deterministic weights, BF16 Q down
projection and W8A8 Q up projection, seven alternating-order rounds of
50 executions per case, slowest rank's wall time, round median. Graph
mode (captured graphs, input values and RoPE buffers refreshed at fixed
addresses before each replay):

| tokens/rank | case | serial (ms) | overlap (ms) | delta |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1024 | balanced | 1138.5 | 877.7 | -22.9% |
| 512 | balanced | 583.2 | 459.6 | -21.2% |
| 128 | balanced | 225.0 | 170.1 | -24.4% |
| 128 | uneven | 225.5 | 173.6 | -23.0% |
| 128 | strided input | 247.5 | 190.4 | -23.1% |
| 128 | empty rank | 225.4 | 170.4 | -24.4% |
| 1 | all inputs empty | 32.4 | 33.0 | +1.8% |

Eager mode is slower with the extra stream context (1089.8 ms -> 1395.4
ms at 1024 tokens/rank), so the win is claimed for graph execution only.
The degenerate all-empty case has nothing to overlap and stays within
noise.

This slowdown is specific to the **eager overlap implementation in the Q
+ gather microbenchmark**; it does not imply that an entire eager model
or PIECEWISE service is slower. Full-model execution includes
inter-layer pipelining, and profiling of continuous PIECEWISE execution
confirmed real Q/communication overlap. The microbenchmark regression
can therefore coexist with the **+2.1% end-to-end output throughput
improvement** observed in the three-round serving A/B below.

#### 3. Communication overlap profile (1024 tokens/rank, 20 replays)

| metric | serial | overlap |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| span | 22.63 ms | 17.35 ms |
| compute union | 12.87 ms | 17.16 ms |
| communication union | 9.58 ms | 10.69 ms |
| overlapped communication | 0 us | 10.67 ms |
| idle | 182 us | 159 us |

#### 4. Correctness parity of the overlapped schedule

The same harness compared both paths against independently constructed
CPU reference tensors over 56 rank-cases and 504 comparison groups (1701
non-empty tensor comparisons) in `eager`, `serial_graph`, and
`overlap_graph` phases, covering uneven lengths, an empty rank,
all-empty logical input, noncontiguous input, and graph replays with
refreshed values:

- all 1701 tensor comparisons bitwise equal (`max_abs = 0`, relative L2
= 0);
- restoration indices compared exactly;
- no phase reported a failure.

This is a kernel-level parity check of the overlapped schedule, not a
model accuracy evaluation.

#### 5. End-to-end serving validation (DeepSeek V4 Flash PD)

2 prefill + 2 decode workers, 32 concurrency, 667 streaming requests per
round, 3 baseline rounds followed by 3 candidate rounds on the same
deployment. These rounds were collected before the switch was
consolidated onto `multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap`; the overlapped
schedule they measure is the one in this PR. 9/9 smoke cases pass in
both phases, and every round reported 667/667 successful requests with 0
failures.

| metric (median of 3 rounds) | baseline | candidate | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Avg TTFT (ms) | 19520.95 | 19068.62 | -2.3% |
| Avg TPOT (ms) | 12.25 | 12.21 | -0.3% |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 930.92 | 950.88 | +2.1% |
| Total throughput (tok/s) | 119414.04 | 121979.34 | +2.1% |
| Avg latency (s) | 31.95 | 31.68 | -0.8% |

That workload is queue-dominated (prefill queue ratio ~0.89, ~1.5 s of
prefill compute against ~13 s of queue time), so the end-to-end delta is
close to run-to-run noise; it is not claimed as a serving-level win. The
microbenchmark and the profile above are the evidence for the
layer-level overlap, and an end-to-end gain needs a prefill-bound
workload.

#### 6. Lint

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (ruff 0.14.0, the version pinned
in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) pass on the touched Python files.

### Checklist

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: the overlap is gated on a
global prefill plus a nonempty local query shard; empty shards keep
participating in every collective, and non-PCP metadata delegates to the
base implementation. Unit tests cover all 12 gate/compression
combinations.
- [ ] **Regression test**: not applicable, this is not a bug fix.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: the Q stream join is in a
`finally` block and
`test_cache_query_preparation_joins_stream_on_failure` injects a failure
at each stage to assert the join still happens.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: unit tests assert the exact
stream/collective call order, and the out-of-tree harness compared both
paths against independent CPU reference tensors with bitwise equality.
- [x] **Performance impact**: microbenchmark and profile results are
attached above; the overlap rides on the existing
`multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap` default and can be disabled with the same
option.

Adds Prefill-Decode (PD) disaggregation deployment guidance to the
Qwen3.8-27B tutorial, which previously only covered single-node online
deployment:

requirements.

troubleshooting path.

## Summary

Add an Atlas 800I A2 (910B4) W4A8 overlay for DeepSeek-V4-Pro: a
four-node
co-located pool, DP4 x TP8 with expert parallelism (EP32), one local DP
rank
per node over all eight devices.

|---|---|---|---|---|

ascend_910b | 4 |

## Deployment coverage

| Strategy | Status |
|---|---|
| multi_node_dep | **verified** (4 nodes, DP4/TP8) |
| single_node_tp / tep / dep | unsupported |
| multi_node_tp / tep / pd_cluster | unsupported |

## Changes

- New file: `recipes/overlays/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro.yaml`
- Adds `ascend_910b` hardware status, an `ascend_w4a8` variant, and a
  `multi_node_dep` preset for a four-node co-located pool
- No changes to any existing recipe

## Test evidence

### Static validation and rendering

node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm-ascend --dir <recipes
dir>
✓ vllm-ascend recipes are valid against the renderer

pnpm test:schema        pass 5   fail 0
pnpm test:overlay       pass 13  fail 0
pnpm test:presets       pass 15  fail 0
pnpm test:hardware      pass 22  fail 0
pnpm test:pd-connectors pass 24  fail 0
pnpm test:guide-html    pass 29  fail 0

`pnpm test:render` was not run locally (needs `sync-sources` which
requires
outbound network on the dev box); it runs in CI.

### NPU smoke and inference correctness

Four Atlas 800I A2 nodes, 8x Ascend 910B4 (64 GB) each,
image `quay.nju.edu.cn/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.32.0rc1`:

- All engines reached `Application startup complete`
- `/health` returned 200 on node 0 (the only API endpoint)
- Single completion request: **HTTP 200 in 55.8 s** (cold); repeat
request 1.4 s
- `1+1=?` with `max_tokens=200` returned content `"2"`
(finish_reason=stop)
- Eight concurrent requests: **8/8 returned 200**, total wall time 72 s
  (≈ one request, confirming the four DP ranks share the load)

### Multi-node distributed connectivity

All four nodes reachable on the NPU side (hccn_tool ping, full mesh, 0%
loss).
DP group formed: `All engine subscriptions received by DP coordinator`.

### Performance benchmarks

Not yet run. Planned with AISBench (tutorial §8).

### Fault tolerance and negative cases

Observed and documented in the hardware note:

- Without `--api-server-count 1` on node 0, vLLM defaults it to
`data_parallel_size` (4), starts four API servers binding ranks that
live on
  other hosts, and **every completion request hangs until timeout while
  `/health` still returns 200**.
- Without `--headless` on nodes 1-3, node 0 aborts with
`Remote engine N must use --headless unless in external or hybrid dp lb
mode`.

## Backward compatibility

New file only; no existing recipe is modified.

## Documentation

`runbook` and `hardware_notes` describe the topology, the two pre-launch
edits,
and the measured per-device footprint (37.72 GiB weights + 12.88 GiB KV
cache).

- [x] `recipe` label added
- [x] Preview deployment succeeds on final head

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds a `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code` overlay with validated **Ascend
910B** (Atlas 800I A2 / 910B4) support for the W4A8 checkpoint in
prefill/decode disaggregation, expressed with the generic PD pools
introduced in #1226.

checkpoint fits a 2P+2D Atlas 800I A2 deployment, but the builder had no
selectable Ascend configuration for this model. The overlay makes the
qualified contract reproducible: two prefill nodes (DP2 x TP8), two
decode nodes (DP4 x TP4), `MooncakeConnectorV1` plus
`AscendStoreConnector` KV transfer, DFlash 15-token drafting, and the
Ascend proxy as the PD front end.

PD is the only supported strategy on 910B; the non-PD strategies are
marked unsupported.

recipes.vllm.ai); no vllm-ascend code, API, or runtime behaviour
changes.
No release note fragment.

1. **Real hardware**: 4 nodes x 8 NPU (32x Ascend 910B4, 64 GB HBM each)
with `Eco-Tech/Kimi-K2.7-Code-w4a8` (revision
`a671b826a7329495a89d6ff70b9c4ea96588c035`) and the Ascend proxy.
Topology: two prefill nodes DP2 x TP8, two decode nodes DP4 x TP4 (local
DP2 per node, ports 7100/7101), `MooncakeConnectorV1` +
`AscendStoreConnector` KV transfer, `z-lab/Kimi-K2.5-DFlash` with 15

[CI][Fix] skip coverage steps when no base ref is available (#22910)

### What this PR does / why we need it?
Fixes #22861 

When a PR target branch does not exist locally or `github.base_ref` is
not available (e.g., PRs targeting a branch that has been deleted, or
certain workflow trigger contexts), the coverage diff steps fail with an
error because `origin/${{ github.base_ref }}` resolves to `origin/`.

This PR adds a `github.base_ref != ''` guard to all five
coverage-related steps in `_selected_tests.yaml`, so they are cleanly
skipped when no base ref is available.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No. This is a CI/workflow infrastructure change only.

### How was this patch tested?
CI testing only. The change is a workflow guard condition; it will be
validated by the CI pipeline on the next PR run.

[Refactor] Drop worker overrides that duplicate upstream (#23047)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`NPUWorker` overrides a set of worker RPCs that upstream
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py::Worker` already implements with the same
behavior. I audited **every** method declared on the class against the
*effective* upstream implementation - `gpu_worker.Worker`, falling back
to `WorkerBase` where the concrete worker does not override it - on
**both** supported vLLM lanes, and deleted the ones that only restate
upstream.

Method: normalized AST comparison (`ast.dump` of each `FunctionDef`,
covering decorators, arguments, annotations, defaults and body) between
the Ascend method and the upstream method that MRO resolves to once the
override is removed, plus a second pass that compares bodies with
annotations stripped to catch annotation-only copies.

Deleted - 13 declarations, all pure delegation to upstream:

| # | method | vs v0.33.0 | vs pinned main `c410543d` | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1-4 | `add_lora`, `remove_lora`, `list_loras`, `pin_lora` | identical
| identical | `return self.model_runner.<m>(...)` |
| 5-7 | `get_model`, `reset_encoder_cache`, `take_draft_token_ids` |
identical | identical | same |
| 8 | `get_supported_tasks` | body + decorators identical | same | only
a redundant quoted return annotation `"tuple[SupportedTask, ...]"`
differed |
| 9 | `reset_mm_cache` | differs (guard) | differs (guard) | upstream
calls `model_runner.reset_mm_cache()` directly; the local `getattr` +
`callable()` guard protected a runner shape that no longer exists |
| 10 | `get_draft_model` | was a `NotImplementedError` stub | same |
every supported runner implements the accessor; MRv2 returns the
speculator's draft model |
| 11-12 | `compute_weight_checksums`, `reset_weights` | differ only in
model access | same | upstream uses `model_runner.get_model()`; MRv2's
`get_model()` is literally `return self.model`, so the local
`_weight_checksum_model()` fallback was dead code |
| 13 | `_weight_checksum_model` (private helper) | Ascend-only |
Ascend-only | became unused with #11-12 |

Imports that only those methods used go away too: `LoRARequest`,
`SupportedTask`, `DraftTokenIds`, and
`compute_tensor_digests`/`zero_weights`.

**The only intended behavior change** is `get_draft_model`: the Ascend
stub used to raise `NotImplementedError`, and it now delegates to the
runner like every other worker. Everything else is byte-for-byte
equivalent, which the NPU runs below confirm. Two further notes:

- `reset_weights` no longer logs the `weight_nz_mode` advisory. The
zeroing behavior is unchanged; the NZ guard that actually rejects
unsupported usage (`_check_nz_disabled`, reached from
`_start_weight_update`) is untouched.
- The `.model`-only runner shape is no longer supported by the
weight-checker RPCs. No such runner exists: the upstream MRv2 runner
defines `get_model()` returning `self.model` on both lanes, and the v1
runner defines it too.

The same audit listed pass-through-looking methods that **do** differ on
at least one lane, so they are deliberately kept: `synchronize_device`
(`torch.npu.synchronize()`), `sample_tokens` (no `@with_gpu_sync_check`
/ `@finish_iteration_timing`), `update_config`, `reload_weights`,
`check_health`, `get_supported_pooling_tasks`, and the remaining
`NotImplementedError` stubs.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No user-visible behavior change beyond removing one
`NotImplementedError` from a worker RPC that no engine path calls on
Ascend. Internal refactor; no release note fragment needed.

### How was this patch tested?

**On real NPU hardware, A/B, under both vLLM lanes** (v0.33.0 tag and
main@`c410543d`), comparing the PR against its parent commit
`7fcd50906`:

- Hardware: Ascend 910 (single die), CANN 9.1.0, torch 2.10.0, torch_npu
2.10.0.post4
- vllm-ascend: `7fcd50906` (base) vs the PR head, selected via
`PYTHONPATH`
- Engine: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, `enable_lora=True`, eager,
`max_model_len=512`, plus a small PEFT adapter (q_proj, r=8) generated
for the test
- `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0` to reach the worker object
in-process, and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` because the container's
prebuilt custom-op set predates this tree (`aclnnAddRmsNormBias`
unavailable). Both settings are applied identically to base and PR, so
the comparison is valid.

| check (same for both vLLM lanes) | base `7fcd50906` | PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `compute_weight_checksums()` over 226 tensors, sha256 of all digests |
`de0b7ab0...` | `de0b7ab0...` (identical) |
| greedy generation, no LoRA | `" Paris. The capital of France is
also..."` | identical |
| greedy generation with the LoRA adapter | `" Paris, and the capital of
Italy is Rome..."` | identical |
| `add_lora` / `pin_lora` / `remove_lora` / `list_loras` | `True` /
`True` / `False` / `[]` | identical |
| `get_model`, `get_supported_tasks`, `take_draft_token_ids`,
`reset_encoder_cache`, `reset_mm_cache` |
`Qwen3ForCausalLM(151936x1024)` / `["generate"]` /
`DraftTokenIds(req_ids=[], draft_token_ids=[])` / `None` / `None` |
identical |
| `reset_weights()` -> all params zero + post-reset checksums | zeroed,
`990b038d...` | zeroed, `990b038d...` (identical) |
| `get_draft_model()` | raises `NotImplementedError` (the removed stub)
| returns `None` (runner's value) - intended |

Unit tests on the same machine, PR tree, both lanes:

- `pytest -q tests/ut/worker/test_worker_weight_checker.py
tests/ut/worker/test_worker_inheritance.py
tests/ut/worker/test_worker_v1.py`
-
`tests/ut/worker/test_worker_inheritance.py::test_get_draft_model_reports_the_runner_drafter`
(added after review) binds the upstream runner method this RPC resolves
to and checks all three states: no speculator, a `DraftModelSpeculator`
carrying a draft module (returned by identity), and a non-draft
speculator.

Also run locally: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `py_compile`, and
the audit re-run -> `0 redundant`, `0 annotation-only` on both lanes.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: `get_draft_model` now covers
configured / absent / non-draft speculator; the deleted pass-throughs
add no new input domain.
- [x] **Regression test**: `test_model_accessors_are_inherited` pins
`NPUWorker.<m> is GPUWorker.<m>` for the remaining accessors, and the
new behavior test pins the one RPC whose behavior changed.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: the removed
`NotImplementedError` path is exactly what the new test replaces.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: tests that asserted deleted
behavior were removed rather than weakened; A/B evidence on real NPU is
in the table above.
- [x] **Performance impact**: not applicable - no hot-path or kernel
change.

commits.message:
[Performance][Model] Integrate AscendC HC forward operator for Qwen4Exp (#22517)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Integrates the AscendC `TextGatedResidual` forward operator into
Qwen4Exp / Qwen3.8-Flash-Next HyperConnections on **main**, porting the
HC integration from #21794.

- Replaces the existing Triton + Linear HC mix pipeline with the fused
operator: grouped Gemma RMSNorm, down/injection projection, SiLU, up
projection and gated mixing.
- Preserves upstream checkpoint names and weight loading. Prepares the
operator's ND projection weights and FP32 norm weights once after
loading, for both the main model and MTP.
- Adds a small Triton combine kernel that consumes the operator's
**final injection weights**, avoiding a second sigmoid/channel scaling
when writing a pending block output back to the residual.

The adapter subclasses upstream `GatedResidual` and uses the existing
model-module bindings; this keeps Ascend-specific execution in the
plugin without copying the upstream model. These bindings can be
replaced by an upstream HC backend extension point when one becomes
available. No model-runner changes or new configuration switches are
introduced.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. When the matching CANN custom operator package and Torch extension
are available, Qwen4Exp HC uses the fused path. If the package is
unavailable, or the configuration uses shared rather than per-branch HC
normalization, the upstream HC implementation remains active.

The fused path requires a CANN custom operator package that provides
`TextGatedResidual` and its matching Torch extension.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Standalone HC performance

A3 single die, BF16 input `[1,M,10240]` (`C=4`, hidden size `2560`, low
rank `320`, `eps=1e-6`, `need_backward=False`). Both implementations use
identical inputs and weights from the original `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next`
checkpoint's layer-0 attention HC. This compares the complete **HC mix
stage**, rather than comparing the fused kernel against only one Triton
kernel.

NPU graph replay with NPU Event timing; initialization, compilation,
warmup and capture excluded. Two scans in opposite M orders, 22 timing
groups per implementation/M, reporting the median of per-group average
latency. Speedup = Triton / HC; lower latency is better. The two
implementations were measured in separate A3 runs; small run-to-run
differences should not be overinterpreted.

| Tokens M | Triton mix (us) | AscendC HC mix (us) | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 21.97 | 25.70 | 0.855x |
| 2 | 25.25 | 26.96 | 0.937x |
| 4 | 27.85 | 27.34 | 1.019x |
| 8 | 31.45 | 28.10 | 1.119x |
| 16 | 39.15 | 28.08 | 1.394x |
| 32 | 48.13 | 34.75 | 1.385x |
| 64 | 56.49 | 41.48 | 1.362x |
| 128 | 68.85 | 52.37 | 1.315x |
| 256 | 91.09 | 64.34 | 1.416x |
| 512 | 138.96 | 106.93 | 1.299x |
| 1024 | 229.40 | 159.89 | 1.435x |
| 2048 | 425.91 | 307.33 | 1.386x |
| 4096 | 959.29 | 589.57 | 1.627x |
| 8192 | 1901.99 | 1258.79 | 1.511x |
| 16384 | 3808.97 | 2300.81 | 1.655x |
| 32768 | 7511.25 | 4187.81 | 1.794x |

Standalone output checks passed at all 16 M values in both scans, eager
and graph mode (`atol=0.02`, `rtol=0.02`). AscendC HC is faster for the
medium and large M values in this run, while M=1 and M=2 remain slower.
Separate device profiling confirmed five mix kernels on the original
path versus one `TextGatedResidual` kernel on the fused path.

#### 128K input / 1K output end-to-end performance

The measured A/B environment was fixed **vLLM `0.33.0+empty`
(`4ba787ec`) and vLLM-Ascend `main` `a41e2ff8` + #21851 `8a398c6b`**
(local merged baseline `5654ae1c`); only the HC adapter differed between
arms. This PR contains the HC port onto current main, **not the changes
from #21851**. The following results are from the pinned A/B experiment
with the `bs-boundary-20261120` package.

- A3 P/D-separated setup; each side used four cards/eight dies with DP4
x TP2 x EP8 x PP1. P always used Triton; only the D HC implementation
was ablated.
- The same pinned vLLM and vLLM-Ascend baseline, model checkpoint,
request token IDs and runtime settings were used for both arms.
- Each request had **131072 input tokens and 1024 output tokens**, with
matched fixed random token IDs, temperature 0 and `ignore_eos=true`. P
prepared the remote KV first; D timing excluded P prefill work.
- The primary capacity metric was steady D output throughput after all
streams started and before any stream completed. Each implementation
searched concurrency independently, and only completed three-round
candidates with mean request TPOT `<=20 ms` were eligible. This is the
appropriate comparison for a TPOT-constrained capacity target;
equal-concurrency results are included as diagnostics.

| Implementation | Selected concurrency | Mean TPOT (ms) | Steady output
throughput (tokens/s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Triton | 31 | 16.251 | 1859.82 |
| AscendC HC | 36 | 16.027 | 1928.37 |
| HC change | - | - | **+3.69%** |

The table compares the best completed three-round candidate observed for
each implementation under the same mean-TPOT constraint. Concurrency is
searched independently because the target is maximum steady D capacity
while mean TPOT remains `<=20 ms`. The measured steady output throughput
improves by **3.69%** with AscendC HC.

#### Matching-shape `kernel_details.csv` evidence

Profiling was collected during actual 128K/1K D requests. Across 16
profiles per arm, both arms had 13,568 complete HC calls with no
unmatched or truncated calls. The matched device-kernel sums were:

| Stage | Local M | Triton (us) | AscendC HC (us) | HC change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Common combine + mix + injection | 8 | 47.42 | 38.90 | **17.96%
lower** |
| Direct mix + injection | 8 | 46.34 | 28.68 | **38.10% lower** |
| Common combine + mix + injection | 2 (D C16) | 34.23 | 33.53 | **2.05%
lower** |
| Common combine + mix + injection | 2 (D C4) | 33.88 | 34.21 | 0.96%
higher |

The Triton values are the sum of the original five-kernel chain; AscendC
values include the new combine kernel plus `TextGatedResidual`. Shapes,
rank, boundary kind and complete iterations were matched. These are
device kernel durations, not whole-request wall times, so local operator
savings do not by themselves establish an end-to-end throughput gain.

#### Integration checks

- The model-specific final-injection Triton combine is implemented in
`vllm_ascend/ops/triton/qwen4_exp/hc.py` and documented in
[`qwen4_exp_hc_combine_final.md`](https://github.com/dlsccc/vllm-ascend/blob/a6159370f568beaa8fc081be776eca8ef703b526/vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/qwen4_exp_hc_combine_final.md).
Its compile-time parameters are fixed by the Qwen4Exp dimensions and
injection mode; token count changes the launch grid. It has no separate
warmup registration.
- Added
`tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_qwen4_exp_hc_fused.py`:
**18 passed** on A3 with the pinned vLLM runtime. Covers mix
with/without injection, pending combine, zero final injection weights,
empty combine and invalid shapes/strides. Representative M values: 1, 4,
512, 1024 and 4096.
- Targeted Ruff, formatting, codespell, typos, Markdown lint,
forbidden-import, boolean-context, logger, long-function and
symbolic-meta checks passed.
- The retained benchmark artifacts include both standalone scans,
per-request E2E JSON, version/package manifests and all-rank
`kernel_details.csv` captures. The detailed benchmark artifacts are
available for review alongside the test results.
- Added `release_notes/fragments/22517.yaml` describing the A3
throughput improvement and the matching CANN operator package / Torch
extension requirement.
#### Triton specialization and recompilation validation

**White-box analysis:** This model-specific final-weight combine uses
`GROUP_DIM=2560`, `HC_COUNT=4`, `BLOCK_SIZE=1024` and the injection mode
as constexpr values. M changes the launch grid and is not a constexpr.
Tensor contents and grid changes do not require new variants; changes to
dtype, constexpr values, stride types or backend specialization classes,
source, compiler or target settings can require compilation. The
operator has no autotuning or separate warmup registration.

**Black-box validation:** A3, Triton-Ascend `3.6.0`, BF16 residual `[M,
10240]`, block output `[M, 2560]`, optional injection `[M, 4]`, with
contiguous rows. JIT calls and the compilation listener recorded shapes,
strides, pointer alignment, compiler signatures, constexpr values and
binary hashes. Process-local JIT misses, disk cache loads and native
binary compilations were counted separately.

| Directed operator validation | New binary compilations | Disk artifact
loads | New specializations |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Empty-cache first calls, both injection modes | 2 | 0 | 2 |
| Two M sweeps after those first calls | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 10 graph captures and 50 replays | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Each of two fresh processes, same disk cache, first calls | 0 | 2 | 0
|
| Each fresh-process sweep, capture and replay phase | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The sweeps covered `M = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024,
2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768` in ascending and descending order, with
both injection modes. Graph capture covered `M = 1, 4, 32, 1024, 8192`
in both modes, with five replays each. Every output matched the FP32
Torch reference followed by the BF16 store exactly (`atol=0`, `rtol=0`).
The two binary hashes corresponded to `HAS_INJECTION=False/True`;
pointer signatures were `*bf16`, row-stride signatures were `i32`,
pointers were 16-byte aligned, and runtime specialization attributes
were empty. M changes added no variants in these runs.

The same production kernel and adapter were observed in the pinned
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next A3 service (`TP8`, EP, MTP3, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`),
using the vLLM/vLLM-Ascend runtime identified above. Executed source
SHA256 values matched PR revision
`25b9290a224711c2cf2eae49056b567aa747a02c`. One serial request completed
with verified input/output token counts of 131072/1024.

| Model-service phase | JIT misses | New binary compilations | Disk
artifact loads | Observed M |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Startup, all 8 workers | 8 | 8 | 0 | 1, 2, 4, 1024 |
| Completed 128K/1K request | 0 | 0 | 0 | 64, 960, 1024 |

Startup produced the same single binary hash independently in each
worker: eight process-local compilations, one unique specialization.
Serving calls and graph replay reused that hash. Observed serving M
values describe JIT launches; captured graph replay can execute kernels
without invoking the Python JIT entry point. These compilation counts
apply to the tested dimensions, dtype, layout and toolchain; they are
separate from the throughput benchmark above.

[Misc] Main2Main v0.34.0 (#22198)

## Summary

Upgrade the vLLM release tag from **v0.33.0** to **v0.34.0** on top of
the already-merged #21469.

The main-pin upgrade landed with #21469, so this PR leaves it untouched
and only completes the release-lane tag migration plus the adaptations
for the differences between the two pins (verified main `c410543d` /
v0.34.0 `62d4bc3c`).

## Markers

| Marker | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.github/vllm-release-tag.commit` | `v0.33.0` (`4ba787ec`) | `v0.34.0`
(`62d4bc3c7e33b1b6c906e233e6af2d3506c482ca`) |

`.github/vllm-main-verified.commit` keeps
`c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15` from #21469; this PR has no
diff there.

### Relationship between the two lanes

`v0.34.0` (`62d4bc3c`) and the verified main pin (`c410543d`) diverge at
`34b780fe`:

- `34b780fe..c410543d`: 388 main commits that are not in v0.34.0
- `34b780fe..62d4bc3c`: 25 release-branch commits that are not in main

Every release-side guard therefore has to be judged against `34b780fe`,
not against the current main pin.

## Adaptation items

Each item below corresponds to a signed-off commit and was checked
against the **v0.34.0 sources**, not only against the scan output.

### 1. Merged-linear padding ownership (#66784) —
`vllm_ascend/ops/{kda_parallel,kimi_kda,linear}.py`

- v0.34.0 state: #66784 is **absent** on `34b780fe`; the merged layer
has no padding-aware loader.
- Fix: the release lane keeps the wrapper-side padding append and the
explicit rejection; `KDAMergedColumnParallelLinear` bypasses
`MergedColumnParallelLinear.__init__` and appends, zeroes and flags the
padding rows itself, so both lanes behave identically.

### 2. Routed-scale kwarg shape (#66859) —
`vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_fused_moe.py`

- v0.34.0 has no `RoutedScaleMode` and still uses
`apply_routed_scale_to_output: bool`.
- Fix: the release lane keeps the boolean kwarg and the 11-argument
`MoERunner` signature; main uses the enum.

### 3. DFlash draft-prepare signature (#66604) —
`vllm_ascend/worker/v2/spec_decode/dflash/speculator.py`

- The v0.34.0 prepare entry point has no `block_stride`.
- Fix: both signatures are kept; the release lane uses
`prepare_with_block_size`, main uses the entry point that takes
`block_stride`.

### 4. Scheduler iteration details

- `IterationDetails` and `_make_cached_request_data(...,
iteration_details=)` exist only on main; v0.34.0 still has the
four-argument call.
- Fix: the details imports and fields are main-only; the release lane
uses the four-argument form. `encoder_input_updates` is kept on both
lanes, and `scheduled_encoder_input_stats` belongs to the release tag so
that v0.34.0 does not silently stop reporting encoder input statistics.

### 5. Eagle/PP aux-hidden-state plumbing —
`vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_deepseek_v2.py`

- `DeepseekV2Model` only adopts `EagleModelMixin` on main.
- Fix: the release lane keeps copying the mixin members in place so that
`_set_aux_hidden_state_layers` / `collect_remote_aux_hidden_states`
exist; the tests exclude the main-only `add_upstream_aux_hidden_states`
/ `upstream_aux_keys` from the v0.34.0 path.

### 6. Weight-update LoRA reset — `vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py`

- `on_target_weights_replaced()` is a main-only hook; v0.34.0 still
calls `reset_lora_state()`.
- Fix: the release lane calls `reset_lora_state()`; main keeps the hook.

### 7. Cumulative PP aux-hidden-state collection —
`vllm_ascend/models/{kimi_k3/kimi_k3,minimax_m3/minimax_m3}.py`

- Main merges the aux slots of earlier PP stages in the runner; v0.34.0
relays them through intermediate tensors.
- Fix: non-first ranks call
`collect_remote_aux_hidden_states(intermediate_tensors)` (which returns
`[]` on main); Kimi K3 recomputes `_aux_upstream_total_cached` after the
capture changes the PP split.

### 8. Unit-test alignment with the v0.34.0 interfaces

- Removed parameterizations that only described deleted `0.33.0`
branches and followed the renamed ABIs: `dp_sync_state`, speculator
`_decode`, `prepare_with_block_size` without `block_stride`.
- Patched `get_pcp_group` at `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.pcp_manager`; added a
PP-group stub for the v0.34.0 `get_pp_safe_draft_load_config()`.
- Where v0.34.0 lacks a main-only helper, the split follows capability
checks or `vllm_version_is("0.34.0")`; all assertions are preserved.

### 9. Model-runner import path — `vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py`

- `GPUModelRunner` lives at `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner` on both
pins and is no longer imported from the pre-split path.

## Full `0.33.0` scan

Every `0.33.0` occurrence in the repository (production code, tests,
examples, docs) was scanned and classified:

| Location | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `vllm_version_is("0.33.0")` in production code and tests | Guard
removed; both lanes take the same path |
| Places where v0.34.0 still needs the old behavior | Rewritten as
`vllm_version_is("0.34.0")` |
| 0.33.0-only modules: `patch_swa_bounded_replay`,
`patch_adaptive_verification`,
`tests/ut/patch/platform/release_scheduler_fixture.py` | Deleted
together with their patch index entries and tests |
| `vllm_ascend/models/step5/{model,sparse_attention}.py` | Removed the
`nvidia` / `common` import branches; both lanes use `common` |
| `examples/offline_DSD_k_tuner/generate_config.py` | Removed the CLI
option `--disable-padded-drafter-batch` (vLLM deleted that option, so it
is retired with v0.33.0 support) |
| `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/prepare_dflash_inputs.md`,
`docs/source/tutorials/models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.md` | ABI/version
wording updated to 0.34.0 |

The same scan also removed guards on older tags that can never fire:
`0.31.0` (`worker/v2/states.py`, `worker/v2/model_runner.py` and one
Qwen4Exp cache test), `0.32.0` (Kimi K3 cache helper) and `0.28.0`
(`patch_kv_cache_utils.py`).

## v0.34.0 ABI adaptations covered by the cleanup

| Area | v0.34.0 change | Downstream fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `_make_cached_request_data` | Four arguments, no `iteration_details` |
Copied scheduler, balancing patch and `patch_pp_mtp` use the
four-argument form |
| `CachedRequestData` / `NewRequestData` | No `resumed_req_ids`;
`replay_start` is native on `NewRequestData` | Deleted
`patch_swa_bounded_replay`; preempted requests re-enter waiting as new
requests |
| ACL graph capture | `capture()` has no `has_lora`; the manager takes
`decode_query_lens` | `aclgraph_utils`, the `_310p` graph wrapper, the
dflash/target-dependent-AR managers and the worker factory updated |
| Rejection sampling | Three-argument sampler; `DraftLogitsCache` rows
are mapped through `draft_logits_row_mapping` |
`rejection_sampler_utils` and the speculator pass the row mapping |
| Mamba spec decode | `create(..., forward_context, ...)`;
`MambaCopyBuffers` removed | Pass the context unconditionally; deleted
the obsolete `uint64` copy-buffer patch |
| Target-dependent AR | Upstream exposes `_decode` | The speculator
overrides `_decode` |
| Kimi Linear config | Native `dsa_config` and `is_dsa_layer` |
`patch_kimi_k31_config` forwards `dsa_config` and delegates to the
native methods |
| OLMoE | The model module moved to the Transformers backend | The
attention patch applies on both lanes |
| Mooncake store | Package name `mooncake_store` → `mooncake` | See the
CI fixes section |
| Dummy inputs embeds | Main's `dummy_inputs_embeds()` gained
`input_ids` | `AscendModelState` forwards `input_ids`; v0.34.0 still
calls the single-argument parent |
| Config hash | Both pins provide `hash_config()` /
`hash_config_cached()` | Mooncake uses the non-cached `hash_config()`,
EPLB uses `hash_config_cached()`, and no local wrapper is kept |

## Baseline sync

The branch keeps merging `origin/main` (current head is shown at the top
of the PR). Conflict policy: when upstream already contains an
equivalent fix, prefer the upstream version and drop the duplicate
change; do not keep dead branches that only serve v0.33.0.

## CI fixes

1. **PP aux relay protocol** — The release lane relays earlier-stage aux
slots through intermediate tensors and the last stage returns `remote +
local`; main returns only its local capture and lets the runner merge.
Both models now pack only local captures into the transport keys, and
the last stage returns remote before local, matching upstream LLaMA
ordering.
2. **PP aux CPU fixture** — The fixture now matches the release mixin:
non-first stages compute the slot base, only the last stage aggregates
the upstream slots, and `collect_remote_aux_hidden_states` is bound.
3. **Resumed-request contract** — vLLM removed `resumed_req_ids`;
resumed requests re-enter through `scheduled_new_reqs` with the full
block list, and the kv-trace test uses that form.
4. **Removed worker attribute** — Dropped the assertion on the removed
`Worker._sleep_saved_draft_buffers` and kept `_sleep_saved_buffers`.
5. **Speculative draft-slot budget** — The DeepSeek V4.1 spec-config
stub now sets `max_num_new_slots_for_drafting=0`.
6. **KDA padding ownership (unified)** — `KDAMergedColumnParallelLinear`
owns the padding allocation and the versioned caller-side append was
deleted.
7. **DSpark aux snapshot** — The release lane clones the aux hidden
state when the additive residual is `None`, so the speculator cannot
read a stale capture that was modified in place.
8. **`cpu-ut (vllm@v0.34.0)` mooncake path** — The module-path guards in
`lookup_key.py` / `ec_connector/mooncake/store_backend.py` pointed at
the wrong version, so the release lane imported
`vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_pool.mooncake_store`, which no longer
exists in v0.34.0; the guards now target `"0.34.0"` and
`mooncake/push_scheduler.py` was updated as well.
9. **`dummy_inputs_embeds` signature** — Main added the `input_ids`
parameter and the override did not forward it, so every main-lane case
raised `TypeError`; the override now forwards it per pin.

## Verification

- `python3 -m py_compile`: all changed files pass
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` (pinned in
`requirements-lint.txt`): all changed files pass
- Repository `0.33.0` leftovers: 4 comment-only mentions (the version
floor note in `kv_cache_dtype_handlers.py`, two historical comments in
`pool_worker.py`, and two test comments); no version branches
- `vllm_version_is(...)` census: 36 × `"0.34.0"`, 2 × `"1.0.0"` (the
sentinel assertion in `tests/ut/test_utils.py`)
- Against `origin/main`: 178 files, +1129 / −3429
- Dual-lane CI (main pin + v0.34.0): see the checks below
